SOLAS V/34, geminin sefere çıkmadan önce: SOLAS V/34 states clearly that the Master must check and approve the passage plan before the ship proceeds to sea. The plan must be prepared berth to berth; the choice of route, adequacy of depth, expected weather and currents, traffic density, anchorages, abort points and contingency anchorages must form integral parts of it. It is not enough for the Master simply to "sign" the plan; the Master is expected actually to review it and confirm that it suits the type of ship, the nature of the voyage and the competence of the crew.
V/34-1 maddesi ise kaptanın seyir emniye: Regulation V/34-1 states clearly that the Master's decisions on the safety of navigation are based on "professional judgement" and that no company, charterer or third party may act in a way that prevents such a decision. In practice this provision is known as the "overriding authority", and it is repeated in section 5.2 of the ISM Code. ISM internal audits look for concrete evidence that the company does not obstruct this authority of the Master.
ISM Code'un 5. maddesi, şirket SMS'inde: Section 5 of the ISM Code requires the company's SMS to define the Master's duties clearly, to give the Master the authority to implement the SMS on board and report deviations to the company, and to confirm the "overriding authority" in writing. Every Master joining a ship carries the company's Master's Standing Orders and Master's Review procedures on board, signed; these documents are checked in internal audits.
Master's Review, ISM'in kalp atışıdır. Y: The Master's Review is the heartbeat of the ISM system. At least once a year (generally every six months), the Master evaluates the effectiveness of the SMS on board and reports deficiencies and suggestions for improvement to the company in writing. These reports are reviewed by the DPA (Designated Person Ashore) and are an input to the company's management review.
Manila değişiklikleriyle birlikte STCW T: With the Manila amendments, STCW Tables A-II/1 and A-II/2 made Bridge Resource Management and Bridge Team Management competences mandatory for Masters and officers. These competences are not just theoretical knowledge; they are behavioural skills: keeping the hierarchy without undermining safety, a "challenge and response" culture, sharing situational awareness, and awareness of human factor risks.
Köprüüstü kaynak yönetiminin başarısız o: In many accidents where bridge resource management failed (Royal Majesty 1995, Sea Empress 1996, Costa Concordia 2012), the common theme is this: the officer of the watch or the pilot had doubts but did not speak up because of the Master's authority. While using their hierarchical power, the modern Master must also build a bridge culture that encourages challenge.
Appraisal, sefere ait tüm verilerin topl: Appraisal is the gathering and evaluation of all the information relevant to the voyage. Publications (Sailing Directions, List of Lights, Tide Tables, Routeing Charts), electronic charts (ENCs) and the necessary T&P NM corrections are checked. Weather forecasts (long and short range), ice reports, piracy areas (HRA, VRA), war risk areas and health authority warnings (yellow fever, malaria, epidemics such as COVID) are compiled at this stage.
Kaptanın bu aşamadaki rolü, 2. Zabit'in: The Master's role at this stage is to read critically the appraisal prepared by the Second Officer (usually the navigating officer). It is the Master's duty to find the points where the route requested by the charterer conflicts with the seasonally safe route and to report them, with reasons, to the company and the charterer. For example, in the North Atlantic winter a great circle may look economical, but in the light of sentinel buoy data and a weather routing service (e.g. WNI, AWT) it may be necessary to keep further south.
Planning aşamasında waypoint'ler belirle: At the planning stage the waypoints are set, and the course alteration points, parallel index lines, contour-following lines and XTD (cross-track distance) limits are defined. There are three critical points the Master must pay particular attention to: the abort point, the contingency anchorage and the point of no return.
Abort point, geminin manevrayı iptal edi: The abort point is the last point at which the ship can abandon the manoeuvre and withdraw to safe water. Beyond it, the manoeuvre can no longer be reversed. The point of no return is the point beyond which it is no longer possible to turn back, because of fuel, tide or the weather window. Failure to mark these points clearly on the plan is one of the most frequently repeated findings in MAIB reports.
Execution, planın gerçek seyir koşulları: Execution is carrying out the plan under actual navigation conditions. Small revisions to the plan may be needed because of changes in the weather, the traffic situation or VTS instructions. These revisions must be entered in the log book and on the passage plan; without the Master's initiative, the officer of the watch cannot change the basic logic of the plan.
Yakıt yönetimi (slow steaming, eco speed: Managing fuel (slow steaming, eco speed), CII performance and the ETA committed to the charterer at the same time is the modern Master's daily arithmetic. If the weather worsens, tactical decisions such as reducing speed, shifting to a safer route or heaving to affect the commercial ETA; but the safety decision always takes priority.
Monitoring, gerçek pozisyonun planlanan: Monitoring is comparing the actual position with the planned route and noticing deviations early. In the ECDIS the route monitoring, XTD, anti-grounding and depth alarms must be set correctly. A situation briefing is always given at watch changes, and standard phrases such as "I have the conn" and "You have the conn" are used.
Kaptan kendisini köprüüstüne çağırma kri: The Master writes the criteria for calling the Master to the bridge clearly in the Master's Standing Orders. Typical criteria: if visibility falls below 2 miles, if the CPA comes within 1 mile, if the ECDIS fails, if bad weather develops differently from expected, on any equipment failure, before a narrow passage, before the expected pilot boarding time, and so on. This list must be tailored to each ship and voyage.
Boğaz, kanal ve dar geçişlerde (Çanakkal: In straits, canals and narrow passages (the Turkish Straits, Suez, Panama, the Singapore Strait, the Dover Strait) the Master is on the bridge in person and usually takes the con directly. The bridge team is standard and drilled: the helmsman at the wheel (autopilot off), the Second Officer monitoring the position, the Third Officer on lookout or assisting, and the Master in command. If there is a pilot, the pilot's advice is assessed; the Master remains in command.
Manevra sırasında \"double watchkeeping\: During manoeuvring the principle of "double watchkeeping" is applied: the position is checked by ECDIS, by radar parallel indexing and by visual bearings. Relying on a single instrument is flagged in MAIB reports as a "single point of failure".
Sınırlı görüş (görüş < 2 mil) anında COL: In restricted visibility (visibility under 2 miles), special measures under COLREG Rule 19 come into force: safe speed, fog signals, engine ready, additional lookout. The Master is called to the bridge at once. Operation of the radar/ARPA, the quality of target tracking (true vs relative motion) and the sea and rain clutter settings must be under the Master's control.
Ağır havada (Beaufort 8 ve üzeri) gemi y: In heavy weather (Beaufort 8 and above) ship handling tactics change: heaving to, scudding, riding it out, seeking shelter. The Master assesses the rolling period and the risks of parametric and synchronous rolling, and alters course and speed according to the GM and the wave period.
Traffic Separation Schemes (TSS), COLREG: Traffic separation schemes (TSS) are governed by COLREG Rule 10. The basic rules are to proceed in the general direction of traffic flow in the lane, to avoid crossing traffic lanes as far as practicable (and, if obliged to cross, to do so on a heading as nearly as practicable at right angles to the general direction of traffic flow), and that only vessels under 20 m and local traffic use the inshore traffic zone between the coast and the TSS. In busy schemes such as Dover, Ushant and the Bosphorus, the Master takes command in person.
Pilot köprüüstüne çıkar çıkmaz Master-Pi: As soon as the pilot reaches the bridge, the Master-Pilot Exchange card is completed: the pilot's route, speed profile, number and arrangement of tugs, tug positions, expected UKC, weather and current, the contingency plan and communication channels are confirmed. This card is not just a bureaucratic form; it is the written evidence of shared situational awareness.
Kaptan komutayı pilota devretmez. Pilotu: The Master does not hand over command to the pilot. The pilot's advice is assessed professionally; advice contrary to safety is rejected. The pilot is an adviser who does not know the ship; the Master is the person who knows the ship best.
Pilot ladder hazırlığı SOLAS V/23 ve IMO: Rigging of the pilot ladder is governed by SOLAS V/23 and IMO Res. A.1045(27). The number of steps, rope size, manropes, securing to strong points on deck (not with magnets), the intermediate platform, lighting, a lifebuoy with a self-igniting light and a responsible officer (usually the Third or Fourth Officer) are the essential elements of the preparation. Faulty pilot ladders are a leading cause of pilot deaths and a reason for detention (deficiency code 30) in PSC inspections.
Weather routing servisleri (örn. AWT, WN: Weather routing services (e.g. AWT, WNI, StormGeo) provide daily route recommendations. These recommendations are not binding; the Master assesses them and accepts or rejects them. A decision to reject is always entered in the log with the reasons. If the charter party has a "follow weather routing" clause, the deviation is reported to the company and the charterer.
Kaptanın yorum becerisi, ham sinoptik ha: The Master's interpretive skill is being able to translate raw synoptic weather data (the 500 hPa pattern, the jet stream, the position of the polar vortex) into ship performance. The modern bridge shows weather and wave data as an ECDIS overlay; but the data is updated every 6 hours and can be wrong at the micro scale.
Tropik siklon yönetiminin temel kuralı \: The basic rule of tropical cyclone management is summarised in the Bowditch chapter on avoiding the storm: in the northern hemisphere the right-hand half (the dangerous semicircle) is dangerous and the left-hand half (the navigable semicircle) relatively safe; in the southern hemisphere it is the other way round. To locate the centre of the cyclone, the Master uses Buys Ballot's law, the rate of fall of pressure, the direction of the swell and the cloud signature.
Modern uydulardan elde edilen besttrack: Best-track data from modern satellites makes the Master's job easier, but uncertainty is high in forecasts beyond 72 hours. With the "1-2-3 rule", the Master adds a safety margin of 100/200/300 NM to the forecast radius at 24/48/72 hours.
ECDIS, kâğıt haritanın yerini almıştır a: The ECDIS has replaced the paper chart, but it is also a potential single point of failure. The Master confirms that all officers have received type-specific training for the make and model of ECDIS on board. ENC updates (weekly), the match between the official chart catalogue and the ENCs for the voyage, and the safety contour, safety depth, shallow contour and deep contour settings are reviewed before the voyage.
ECDIS'in over-reliance riski MAIB tarafı: The risk of over-reliance on ECDIS has been reported many times by the MAIB (CFL Performer 2008, Ovit 2013). The Master requires the ECDIS to be used not on its own but cross-checked with radar parallel indexing, visual bearings and GPS.
Radar tuning (gain, sea clutter, rain cl: Radar tuning (gain, sea clutter, rain clutter), antenna height, blind sectors and sector checks are under the Master's supervision. ARPA target acquisition quality (true motion vs relative motion), CPA/TCPA limits and the use of trial manoeuvres are handled by the officer of the watch; the Master ensures this through training and supervision.
AIS, COLREG manevra yorumu için tek başı: AIS alone is not sufficient for interpreting COLREG manoeuvres; it must be confirmed by radar. In areas where AIS spoofing or wrong data is common (the Black Sea, the Persian Gulf), the Master requires extra caution.
Overriding authority; charterer'in fast: The overriding authority is used in situations such as a charterer's request for fast steaming, cost pressure from the company, a terminal operator pressing for haste, a charterer's order to an unsafe port, a faulty pilot manoeuvre, or pressure to sail with deficient equipment. The decision is justified as "professional judgement" and reported to the company in writing.
Bu yetkinin kullanılması nadiren popüler: Using this authority is rarely a popular decision; but the Master not holding back when he or she should have is the common theme of fatal accidents. In ISM internal audits companies examine "records of the use of the overriding authority"; even its never having been used is sometimes seen as a sign of a "culture of fear".
Karar alındığında: log book'a tam metin: When the decision is taken, it is written out in full in the log book, reported by email to the company's DPA and operations manager, and notified to the charterer through the NOR/SOF. This triple record is the strongest evidence protecting the Master and the company in any later legal dispute.
Kaptan, Giglio Adası'na yakın \"salute\": The Master ran the ship aground while making a "salute" manoeuvre close to the island of Giglio. 32 dead. The investigation revealed that the manoeuvre was not in the passage plan, the unsafe distance from the shore, a lack of BRM and the chaotic management of the Master-pilot relationship.
Ders: planlanmamış manevra yapılmaz. Yap: Lesson: unplanned manoeuvres are not made. If one is to be made, a written risk assessment is prepared and approved by the company.
Kasırga rotasında ısrar, 33 ölü. Ders: w: Insisting on a route into a hurricane: 33 dead. Lesson: the advice of the weather routing service cannot be ignored; a junior officer's challenge must not be suppressed.
Mauritius açıklarında karaya oturma, doğ: Grounding off Mauritius: approaching the coast for a birthday celebration and an unplanned route to get a Wi-Fi signal. Lesson: any deviation from the passage plan needs written justification; "small" personal motives trigger major accidents.
Standing orders, kaptanın gemi süresince: The standing orders set out in writing the behaviour the Master expects from the officers of the watch throughout his or her time on board. All officers sign them. Typical content: the criteria for calling the Master, the rules for using the autopilot, when to call the helmsman, the conditions for posting an additional lookout, discipline in writing the log book, alarm management and the GMDSS test schedule.
Her akşam kaptan, ertesi 24 saatlik sefe: Every evening the Master writes specific instructions for the next 24 hours of the voyage in the night order book: the expected course alteration points, the expected weather, traffic information, when to call the Master and ETA updates. Night orders are the most practical tool for helping the officer of the watch with decisions during the night.
Mevzuat sürekli güncellenir (IMO MSC ve: The regulations are updated continuously (the IMO MSC and MEPC each meet twice a year). The Master regularly follows amendments to SOLAS, MARPOL and STCW, IMO circulars, P&I bulletins and MAIB and TSB reports. Company bulletins, vetting reports (RightShip, OCIMF SIRE) and class technical bulletins are the Master's daily reading list.
ISM Code 16 madde üzerine kuruludur; bun: The ISM Code is built on 16 sections, covering subjects such as the company policy (section 2), company responsibilities (section 3), the Designated Person Ashore — DPA (section 4), the Master's responsibility and authority (section 5), resources and personnel (section 6), development of plans for shipboard operations (section 7), emergency preparedness (section 8), reporting of non-conformities, accidents and hazardous occurrences (section 9), maintenance (section 10), documentation (section 11) and company verification, review and evaluation (section 12). For the Master, section 5 (Master's Responsibility and Authority) and section 9 (reporting) are the backbone of daily practice.
Madde 5, şirket SMS'inde kaptanın görevl: Section 5 requires the company's SMS to define the Master's duties clearly, to give the Master the authority to implement the SMS on board and to report deviations to the company, and to confirm the "overriding authority" in writing. In other words, the company must explicitly give the Master the authority to put safety and environmental protection above any commercial consideration. This written confirmation is among the first pieces of evidence looked for in internal and external audits.
Document of Compliance (DOC) şirkete ver: The Document of Compliance (DOC) is issued to the company and covers the types of ship it operates (bulk carrier, oil tanker, chemical tanker, gas carrier, container ship, passenger ship and so on). The Safety Management Certificate (SMC) is issued to the ship and shows that the ship is operated in accordance with the company's SMS. The ship must carry a copy of the DOC, because the SMC rests on a valid DOC. The Master always verifies that the ship's type is listed on the DOC; otherwise the SMC may be considered invalid.
DOC 5 yıl geçerlidir ve yıllık doğrulama: The DOC is valid for 5 years and is subject to annual verification (within a window of ±3 months). The SMC is also valid for 5 years, but its intermediate verification takes place between the second and third anniversary dates. The Master follows these windows; a late verification of certificates is a reason for detention in Port State Control (PSC) inspections. Interim certificates (Interim DOC/SMC) are issued for 6 months (12 months with an extension) in cases such as the delivery of a new ship or a change of company.
SMS, gemide somut olarak bir dizi el kit: On board, the SMS lives concretely as a set of manuals, checklists, forms and records: the Safety Management Manual, procedures for critical operations (enclosed space entry, hot work, mooring, bunkering, navigation), risk assessment templates, the permit-to-work system and the records archive. The Master's task is to confirm that these documents are at the latest revision on board (controlled document register), that old revisions have been withdrawn, and that the crew can access the relevant procedures.
Kaptan, gemiye yeni katılan her personel: The Master checks that familiarisation is carried out in accordance with the SMS for every new crew member joining the ship; this is a direct requirement of ISM section 6. No one may be assigned to a watch or a critical operation until familiarisation is complete. This check is an area that PSC and vetting inspections often look at, especially on ships with high crew turnover.
Modern SMS, \"her kritik ve rutin dışı o: A modern SMS is based on the principle of a written risk assessment before every critical and non-routine operation. The common methodology is a 5×5 risk matrix: likelihood (1–5) times severity (1–5) equals the risk score. High-scoring jobs (generally above 12) are either cancelled or brought down to an acceptable level with additional barriers (control measures). The Master checks that the risk assessment team is made up of the right people (including those who will actually do the job) and that the ALARP principle (as low as reasonably practicable) is observed.
Dinamik risk değerlendirmesi (dynamic ri: Dynamic risk assessment is the immediate re-assessment of a job when conditions on site change (the weather worsens, equipment fails, the team becomes tired). The toolbox talk (a short briefing before the job) is the practical tool for this. The Master builds a just culture that clearly establishes that every crew member has stop-work authority and that anyone who uses it will not be penalised.
Management of Change (Değişim Yönetimi),: Management of Change ensures that any permanent or temporary change on board (equipment, procedures, crew composition, software, structure) is assessed in a controlled way. For example, if the type of a critical valve is to be changed, a procedure is to be bypassed or an experienced officer is to be replaced by a new one, the MOC process is triggered. The aim is to prevent a change that "looks small" from creating hidden risks.
MOC formu; değişikliğin tanımı, gerekçes: The MOC form covers the description of the change, its justification, the risk assessment, the approvals required (the Master and usually the company/DPA), the implementation steps and a review after the change. TMSA 3 (OCIMF's self-assessment for tankers) explicitly measures MOC as a performance indicator. Through MOC discipline, the Master prevents a temporary solution (e.g. a workaround for faulty equipment) from becoming a permanent norm.
Permit-to-Work (PTW) sistemi; enclosed s: A permit-to-work (PTW) system is mandatory for high-risk work such as enclosed space entry, hot work (welding/grinding), work aloft, work overboard and electrical isolation (LOTO — lock out, tag out). The permit carries the signatures of the person authorising the work (usually the Master or an officer appointed by him or her), the person doing it and the person verifying it; it is valid for a limited time and is closed when the work is finished.
Enclosed space entry, denizcilikteki ölü: Enclosed space entry is one of the leading causes of fatal accidents at sea. SOLAS III/19.3.3 requires enclosed space entry and rescue drills at least every two months for crew members with entry or rescue duties. Before the permit, the atmosphere is tested (O2 20.9%, LEL 0%, H2S/CO within tolerances), continuous ventilation is provided, and a standby person and resuscitation equipment are kept ready. The Master applies without compromise the rule that no enclosed space is entered without being tested.
ISM madde 12, şirketin SMS'i en az yılda: ISM section 12 requires the company to verify the SMS by internal audit at least once a year. These audits are carried out by (trained) internal auditors independent of the area being audited. On the ship's side, the Master ensures that records are ready for the audit, procedures have been applied and the team can answer questions. The internal audit should be positioned as a tool for "improvement", not "punishment"; otherwise findings are hidden and the system goes blind.
Denetim bulguları üç kategoriye ayrılır:: Audit findings fall into three categories: observation, non-conformity (NC) and major non-conformity (major NC). For each finding a root cause analysis is made (e.g. 5 Whys, fishbone diagram) and corrective and preventive actions are defined. Superficial close-outs such as "personnel were warned" are rejected by the auditor.
Uygunsuzluk (NC), SMS'in bir gerekliliği: A non-conformity (NC) is an observed situation in which a requirement of the SMS has not been met (e.g. a missing drill record). A major non-conformity is a serious finding that poses a serious threat to safety or the environment, points to a systematic failure, or arises from several minor NCs together (e.g. emergency equipment not working, a critical procedure never being applied). A major NC directly endangers the validity of the DOC or SMC.
Major NC, denetim bitmeden veya çok kısa: A major NC must be closed before the end of the audit or within a very short time; otherwise the certificate may be suspended and the ship may be prevented from sailing. In the case of a major NC, the Master informs the DPA immediately, takes immediate containment measures and implements the permanent corrective action plan within the time set. A serious ISM-related finding in a PSC inspection is recorded as an "ISM-related detention" and brings additional inspection pressure on the company's whole fleet.
Near-miss (ramak kala olay), bir kazaya: A near miss is an event that could have led to an accident but passed without consequences. MSC-MEPC.7/Circ.7 encourages near-miss reporting, because beneath every serious accident lie dozens of near misses and hundreds of unsafe acts (the Heinrich/Bird pyramid). The Master creates a non-blaming environment that encourages the crew to report near misses; a high number of near-miss reports is not bad but, on the contrary, a sign of a healthy safety culture.
Düzeltici aksiyon döngüsü PDCA (Plan-Do-: The corrective action cycle works on PDCA (Plan-Do-Check-Act) logic: the event is reported, the root cause found, the action defined and implemented, and its effectiveness verified (effectiveness check). If the effectiveness check is skipped, the same event recurs. The Master is the person who follows whether the closed actions have really solved the problem; this tracking log is examined in audits.
ISM madde 8, şirketin olası acil durumla: ISM section 8 requires the company to identify potential emergencies (fire, collision, grounding, flooding, pollution, man overboard, abandoning ship, serious machinery failure, security incidents and so on) and to prepare a response plan for each. These plans are kept on board as the Emergency Response/Contingency Manual and are documents the Master can access every day and knows by heart. Each plan must make the command structure, roles, communication flow and first response steps clear.
Kaptan, müster listesinin (muster list —: The Master confirms that the muster list (SOLAS III/8) is up to date, that every crew member knows his or her duties in an emergency (fire party, rescue party, first aid, preparing liferafts) and that the equipment assignments (radios, EEBDs, hoses) are correct. When the crew changes, the muster list is updated at once.
SOLAS, belirli drill'leri zorunlu frekan: SOLAS requires certain drills to be held at mandatory intervals: abandon ship and fire drills every month (SOLAS III/19.3.2); every week on passenger ships (SOLAS III/30.2). Training in the use of the ship's life-saving and fire-fighting appliances is given to crew joining the ship within two weeks at the latest (SOLAS III/19.4.1). Enclosed space entry and rescue drills are held at least every two months (III/19.3.3), lifeboat launching and manoeuvring at least every three months (III/19.3.4.3), and rescue boat launching monthly as far as reasonable and in any case at least every three months (III/19.3.4.6). The Master plans this schedule and ensures that the drills are realistic and not just "on paper".
ISPS Code iki bölümden oluşur: Part A zo: The ISPS Code has two parts: Part A contains the mandatory requirements and Part B the recommendatory guidance (although many flag states also make Part B mandatory). The key players are the CSO (Company Security Officer, ashore), the SSO (Ship Security Officer, usually a deck officer) and the PFSO (Port Facility Security Officer). The Master is the SSO's superior and has overall responsibility for the security of the ship.
Kritik bir prensip: ISPS, kaptanın emniy: A critical principle: the ISPS Code confirms the Master's overriding authority in safety and security decisions. SOLAS XI-2/8 states clearly that if safety and security requirements conflict, the Master has the authority to give priority to safety. In other words, if a security request (e.g. carrying out a particular search) would endanger the safety of the ship, the Master may refuse it.
Ship Security Plan (SSP), her gemi için: The Ship Security Plan (SSP) is a document prepared for each ship on the basis of the Ship Security Assessment (SSA) and approved by the flag state (or an authorised RSO). The SSP defines access control, restricted areas, security equipment, the measures to be taken at each security level, the SSAS procedure and the response to security incidents. The SSP is a confidential document; even a PSC inspector may not see certain parts of it (only certain operational items may be shown).
Kaptan ve SSO, SSP'nin güncel, manipülas: The Master and the SSO ensure that the SSP is up to date and protected against tampering (with authorised access if it is electronic), and that the security equipment on board (CCTV, lighting, access barriers, metal detector) is in working order. The Continuous Synopsis Record (CSR — SOLAS XI-1/5) keeps the ship's "identity history" (flag, name, owner, ISM/ISPS certificate history) and is kept on board.
ISPS üç güvenlik seviyesi tanımlar. Sevi: The ISPS Code defines three security levels. Level 1 (normal): minimum appropriate protective measures are maintained at all times. Level 2 (heightened): additional protective measures are maintained for a period of time because of a heightened risk. Level 3 (exceptional): further specific protective measures are maintained for a limited period when a security incident is probable or imminent. The security level is set by the flag state or the port state authorities; the ship applies the higher of the level of the port it is in and the level set by its own flag.
Seviye yükseldiğinde kaptan ve SSO, SSP': When the level is raised, the Master and the SSO put into effect the measures defined in the SSP for that level: reducing the number of access points, tightening identity checks, increasing searches of baggage and stores, more frequent patrols and more intensive watch on the seaward side (anti-piracy/anti-stowaway watch). Changes of level and the measures applied are recorded; these records are reported to the port authority and the company.
Declaration of Security (DoS), gemi ile: A Declaration of Security (DoS) is a document confirming in writing how security responsibilities are shared between the ship and a port facility (or another ship). A DoS is requested especially when the security levels differ, when the ship is at a facility that does not apply the ISPS Code, during a high-risk operation (e.g. STS — ship-to-ship transfer) or after a security incident. The SSO or the Master has the authority to request a DoS when necessary.
DoS; her tarafın hangi güvenlik önlemini: The DoS states which security measures each party undertakes (access control, cargo checks, patrols and so on), its period of validity and the signatories. At a facility that does not apply, or only weakly applies, the ISPS Code, the Master clarifies the limits of responsibility with a DoS and takes additional measures on the ship's side. DoS records are among the security records the ship must keep for a minimum period.
Ship Security Alert System (SSAS), SOLAS: The Ship Security Alert System (SSAS) is mandatory on certain ships under SOLAS XI-2/6. When there is a security threat (piracy, terrorism, hijacking), the SSAS sends a silent alert directly to the company security contact and/or the flag state authority, without sounding an alarm on board and without alerting nearby ships. There are at least two activation points, one on the bridge and the other in a concealed location. The activation points are protected to prevent false alerts.
Kaptan ve SSO, SSAS test prosedürünü (ge: The Master and the SSO know the SSAS test procedure (usually coordinated in advance with the authorities) and test the system periodically. An SSAS alert triggered by mistake must be cancelled at once by notifying the centres concerned; otherwise an unnecessary search and rescue operation or military intervention may be triggered. The SSAS message contains the ship's identity, its position and an indication that its security is under threat.
Korsanlık/armed robbery riski olan bölge: In areas with a risk of piracy or armed robbery (the Gulf of Aden, the Gulf of Guinea, the approaches to the Singapore Strait and so on), the Best Management Practices (BMP) are applied. Preparation covers registration and reporting with UKMTO and MSCHOA, maximising speed and freeboard, physical hardening (razor wire, water curtains, closing off access), an enhanced lookout arrangement and preparing a citadel (safe muster point). The Master updates the risk assessment and briefs the crew before entering the area.
Citadel, mürettebatın saldırı anında çek: The citadel is a protected area, impossible to enter from outside and with means of communication, to which the crew withdraw during an attack. The citadel principle is that no military rescue can be launched unless the whole crew is inside and accounted for and secure communication with the outside has been established. Carrying privately contracted armed security personnel (PCASP) depends on flag and port state permission, company policy and strict rules for the use of force; the Master is the person who applies this framework on board.
Bir güvenlik olayı (yetkisiz erişim giri: In a security incident (an attempt at unauthorised access, a suspicious package or person, a bomb threat, a stowaway, an attack), the Master applies the response steps in the SSP, coordinates with the CSO and the PFSO, and notifies the relevant state authorities (flag/port) and, where necessary, uses the SSAS. After the incident detailed records are kept and the root cause is assessed; the SSP or procedures may be updated to prevent a recurrence (this is where the ISM and ISPS systems meet).
ISM (safety) ve ISPS (security) farklı s: Although ISM (safety) and ISPS (security) arise from different conventions, on board they should be run as a single integrated management system. The risk assessment methodology, document control, audit logic, corrective action cycle and record-keeping discipline are the same in both. Many companies bring these two systems together (sometimes with the MLC and ISO 14001 environmental management) under a single integrated management manual. The Master ensures that these systems work as a single discipline and not as separate silos.
Pratikte bir olay hem emniyet hem güvenl: In practice an incident can have both a safety and a security dimension: for example, an unauthorised person entering the engine room is both a security breach and a safety risk. The Master manages the reporting flow and the response from both points of view. The annual management review assesses the performance indicators of both systems together (KPIs: number of NCs, drill quality, near-miss rate, number of security incidents).
Seyir emniyetinin nihai sorumluluğu, kap: The ultimate responsibility for the safety of navigation gives the Master both great authority and a great burden. This authority is not a "privilege of rank"; it is a professional position earned anew every day with every decision. SOLAS V/34, ISM 5.2 and STCW define this authority not to protect the Master but to protect safety at sea. A sensible Master builds a bridge culture in which he or she never has to "use" this authority; but uses it without hesitation the moment it is needed.
The quality of a drill bears the Master's signature. An effective drill includes a realistic scenario, an unexpected complication (e.g. "this liferaft is defective, use the alternative"), timing, and a debrief afterwards. "What went well / what to improve" is written in the drill records and deficiencies are turned into corrective actions. Beyond seeing the record, a PSC inspector can test real competence by saying "show me".
Kaptan, ISPS güvenlik kayıtlarını (güven: The Master keeps the ISPS security records (changes of security level, DoS documents, security drills and exercises, equipment tests, incident reports) for the specified minimum period and keeps them available for PSC and security inspections. Security drills are held at least every three months, and more comprehensive exercises (with the participation of the company or the PFSO) at least once a year.
DPA (Designated Person Ashore), ISM madd: Under ISM section 4, the DPA (Designated Person Ashore) is a direct link between the Master and the highest level of the company's management. When there is a safety or environmental concern, the Master can bypass the hierarchy and go directly to the DPA; this access can never be blocked. Similarly, the CSO is the Master's counterpart ashore on security matters. The Master ensures that these two channels work openly, quickly and with records.
Master's Review (kaptanın SMS değerlendi: The Master's Review (the Master's evaluation of the SMS) is the Master's periodic feedback on the effectiveness of the system on board and a critical input to the management review. Here the Master reports honestly any gaps of the "it's on paper but not working in practice" kind; this honesty is the only way for the system really to improve. A Master's Review that hides the reality on board is one of the most dangerous management failures.
Port State Control (Paris MOU, Tokyo MOU: A Port State Control inspector (Paris MOU, Tokyo MOU, USCG and others) tests the ship's ISM and ISPS compliance both through documents and on site. For ISM: the validity of certificates, drill records, equipment maintenance records and whether there are open NCs; for ISPS: the validity of the ISSC (International Ship Security Certificate), the gangway watch and access control, the security records and the presence of the CSR are examined. If there are "clear grounds", a more detailed inspection is opened.
Kaptan, denetim öncesi bir self-assessme: Before an inspection the Master carries out a self-assessment (PSC self-assessment) and closes beforehand the items that frequently lead to detention (defects in LSA/FFA equipment, missing records, emergency equipment not working, security gaps). A serious systemic ISM finding leads to the ship being detained and the company falling into "targeted" status, which brings an additional inspection burden on the whole fleet.
Tankerlerde OCIMF SIRE 2.0 vetting denet: For tankers, OCIMF SIRE 2.0 vetting inspections and the company-level TMSA 3 self-assessment are extensions of ISM/ISPS that have become mandatory in practice in commercial life. A tanker may fail to find cargo because of a bad SIRE report despite valid certificates. The Master masters the SIRE question bank and ensures that the records and practices on board are consistent with the TMSA elements (e.g. MOC, risk management, navigation safety).
Kuru yük tarafında RightShip değerlendir: On the dry cargo side, the RightShip assessment acts as a similar gatekeeper. The Master's daily discipline (records kept up to date, equipment in working order, a competent team) is reflected directly in these external inspections in the fleet's commercial competitiveness. In other words, ISM/ISPS is not only a legal matter but a matter of commercial survival.
ISM ve ISPS, denetimde \"kağıt göstermek: ISM and ISPS do not exist for "showing paper" in an inspection; they live as a system that protects the crew, the ship and the environment when an accident or a security incident happens on board. The strength of this system comes from the Master owning it not as a bureaucratic burden but as a discipline and a just culture that support his or her decisions. Certificates may hang on the wall; but what really makes ISM/ISPS work is the honest reporting, document discipline and the culture that rewards the courage to "stop work", which the Master builds every day.
MLC içeriği beş Title altında düzenlenir: The content of the MLC is organised under five Titles: Title 1 — minimum requirements for seafarers to work on a ship (minimum age, medical certificate, training, recruitment); Title 2 — conditions of employment (SEA, wages, hours of work and rest, leave, repatriation, compensation for the ship's loss, manning, career); Title 3 — accommodation, recreational facilities, food and catering; Title 4 — health protection, medical care, welfare and social security; Title 5 — compliance and enforcement (DMLC, inspection, complaints, PSC). The Master is the "supervisor on site" for each of the five Titles.
Kaptanın rolü, standartları yalnızca \"b: The Master's role is not only to "know" the standards but to ensure that they are actually applied on board, to prove it and to correct deviations. Since the philosophy of the MLC is "decent working and living conditions for seafarers", the Master's leadership style directly determines whether these rights are realised.
Her MLC kapsamındaki gemi, Maritime Labo: Every ship covered by the MLC carries a Maritime Labour Certificate and, attached to it, a Declaration of Maritime Labour Compliance (DMLC). DMLC Part I is issued by the flag state and summarises the relevant requirements of national law. DMLC Part II is prepared by the shipowner and describes the concrete measures applied on board for each item in Part I; the flag state approves it.
Kaptan, DMLC Part II'yi günlük yönetimin: The Master uses DMLC Part II like a "user manual" for daily management: it states which procedure and which form are applied, and how often, on each subject. If a PSC inspector finds a contradiction between what is observed on board and the DMLC Part II declaration, this counts as a non-conformity. Even if the certificate is valid, the ship can be detained if there is an actual violation.
MLC, gemide çalışmak için asgari yaşı 16: The MLC sets the minimum age for working on a ship at 16; there are restrictions on night work and hazardous work for seafarers under 18. Every seafarer must hold a valid medical fitness certificate (generally valid for 2 years, 1 year for those under 18); a separate period applies for duties requiring colour vision. The Master personally verifies the validity of the medical and STCW certificates of every seafarer joining the ship.
Süresi dolmuş medikal veya eksik STCW se: An expired medical certificate or a missing STCW certificate is a violation of both the MLC and STCW and a reason for PSC detention. The Master follows certificate expiry dates in crew change planning; if a seafarer's certificate will expire during the voyage, renewal or replacement is coordinated in advance.
MLC, denizcilerin ücretsiz işe alınmasın: The MLC guarantees that seafarers are recruited free of charge: a seafarer may not be charged for finding a job (the manning agency's commission may not be passed on to the seafarer). Using licensed or regulated recruitment and placement services is essential. The Master watches that seafarers joining the ship have been employed through a legal and transparent process and have not come in situations resembling debt bondage.
Modern slavery ve insan kaçakçılığı risk: The risk of modern slavery and human trafficking is real in shipping; a breach of the free recruitment principle is the first sign of it. In a suspicious case the Master coordinates with the DPA and the CSO; keeping a seafarer's passport against his or her will (passport retention) is a violation of the MLC and of human rights.
Her denizci, imzalı bir Seafarers' Emplo: Every seafarer must have a signed Seafarers' Employment Agreement (SEA); one copy is held by the seafarer and one is kept on board. The SEA contains the identities of the parties, the start date and duration, the position, wages, hours of work, annual leave, repatriation rights, health and social security, and the conditions for termination. The Master verifies that the SEA of every seafarer on board is present, legible and valid; it is one of the first documents PSC asks for.
Toplu iş sözleşmesi (CBA, örn. ITF/IBF k: If there is a collective bargaining agreement (CBA, e.g. under ITF/IBF), the SEA refers to it and the CBA is kept on board. The Master ensures consistency between the SEA and actual practice (wages, position, hours of work); if a seafarer is employed in a different position from the one stated in the SEA or is underpaid, this is a violation of the MLC.
MLC ve STCW A-VIII/1, dinlenme saatleri: The MLC and STCW A-VIII/1 give two alternative limits for hours of rest. Minimum rest: at least 10 hours of rest in any 24-hour period and at least 77 hours in any 7-day period. Rest may be divided into no more than two periods, one of which must be at least 6 hours long, and the interval between consecutive periods of rest must not exceed 14 hours. Alternatively, the ILO 180 maximum hours of work (no more than 14 in any 24 hours and 72 in any 7 days) may be applied; the flag state states which it has chosen in the DMLC.
Kaptan, vardiya planını (watch system) b: The Master sets up the watch system in the light of these limits and has the rest hour records kept daily. Port operations, drills, PSC/vetting inspections and emergencies carry a high risk of upsetting rest hours. Fatigue is among the leading causes of accidents in MAIB reports; the Master plans honestly so as not to create a crew that is "compliant on paper but tired in reality".
Ödenmemiş maaş (wages outstanding), PSC: Unpaid wages (wages outstanding) are treated by PSC as a serious violation of the MLC and can lead to the ship being detained; the ITF also inspects ships in port for unpaid wages and, if necessary, has them arrested. When the Master notices a payment problem, he or she reports it at once to the DPA; the shipowner's financial difficulties cannot delay a seafarer's wages, and this situation is an early sign of the risk of abandonment.
MLC, denizcinin belirli durumlarda ücret: The MLC guarantees the seafarer's right to be repatriated free of charge to his or her home country (or an agreed place) in certain circumstances: expiry of the SEA, illness or injury, loss of the ship, justified termination of the SEA by the shipowner or the seafarer, the seafarer being sent to a war zone, and so on. The maximum period of service on board (after which the right to repatriation arises, generally 11 months) is set by flag state law. It is prohibited to recover repatriation costs from the seafarer (by advance deductions), except in cases of serious default by the seafarer.
Kaptan, repatriation hakkı doğan denizci: For a seafarer whose right to repatriation has arisen, the Master coordinates with the agent and the company; the air ticket, visa, transit and settlement of wages are arranged. During the COVID-19 period hundreds of thousands of seafarers were stranded on ships because of the "crew change crisis"; this was a period in which the MLC's repatriation provision was tested on a global scale, and joint IMO/ILO statements stressed seafarers' status as "key workers".
MLC 2014 değişiklikleri (2017'de yürürlü: The 2014 amendments to the MLC (in force since 2017) introduced two new mandatory financial securities: (1) insurance or a guarantee covering repatriation, outstanding wages and essential needs in the event of the seafarer's abandonment; (2) financial security for contractual compensation arising from occupational injury, illness or death. The ship must carry the certificates proving this security (usually from a P&I Club) and post them in a visible place.
Abandonment, armatörün denizciyle bağı k: Abandonment is defined as the shipowner severing its ties with the seafarer (failing to cover the cost of repatriation, failing to pay wages for at least 2 months, or leaving the seafarer without support). When a risk of abandonment appears on board (late wages, supplies cut off, the company going silent), the Master detects it early and informs the seafarers of their right to apply to the insurer named in the financial security certificate; the ILO tracks these cases in a public database.
MLC Title 3, kamara büyüklüğü, havalandı: MLC Title 3 sets concrete standards for cabin size, ventilation/air-conditioning, lighting, noise and vibration limits, beds, sanitary facilities (ratio of toilets and showers), laundry, the hospital and recreational facilities. These standards are largely met at the building or refit stage, but the Master is responsible for maintaining them (maintenance, cleanliness, function). Air-conditioning not working, noise above the limits or too few toilets and showers are real welfare problems.
Kaptan, periyodik konaklama denetimi (ac: The Master carries out periodic accommodation inspections; the MLC requires these inspections to be carried out frequently (generally at least weekly, regularly under most SMSs) and recorded. The inspection covers cleanliness, working fittings, pest and rodent control, and the condition of the laundry and the hospital. Findings are closed with corrective action.
MLC, denizcilere ücretsiz, yeterli mikta: The MLC guarantees that seafarers are provided free of charge with food and drinking water of sufficient quantity and nutritional value, respecting cultural and religious differences. Catering staff (the cook) must be trained and over 18; on ships with a prescribed manning of more than 10, a qualified (certified) ship's cook is required. The Master checks the variety of the menu, the adequacy of portions, the food stock, the cold chain and the hygiene of storage.
İçme suyu kalitesi (potability) sağlık a: Drinking water quality (potability) is critical for health; tank chlorination, periodic water tests and cleaning of the hydrophore system are followed. Galley hygiene is managed on HACCP principles: preventing cross-contamination, temperature control (refrigerator below 4 °C, freezer below −18 °C), date control and personal hygiene. A food-borne outbreak (gastroenteritis) can paralyse operations on a ship.
MLC, denizcilere karadakine eşdeğer, müm: The MLC aims to give seafarers medical care comparable to that ashore, as far as possible free of charge. A ship has a medicine chest, a medical guide (the WHO International Medical Guide for Ships or equivalent) and access to medical advice by radio or satellite (TMAS — Telemedical Maritime Assistance Service). Ships carrying 100 or more persons on international voyages of more than three days carry a doctor; on other ships an officer in charge of medical care (usually the Master or the Second Officer, trained in medical care under STCW) is designated.
Kaptan, ilaç dolabının envanterini, son: The Master checks the inventory of the medicine chest, the expiry dates and the narcotics records; missing or expired medicines are replaced in port. In a serious case, TMAS is consulted and, if necessary, a MEDEVAC is arranged (by helicopter or by deviating to the nearest port); this decision lies within the Master's overriding authority and is taken despite any commercial loss.
Title 4, denizcilerin karada ve gemide r: Title 4 supports seafarers' access to welfare facilities ashore and on board (seafarers' clubs, recreation, communication); shipowners and port states are encouraged to provide welfare facilities. In modern times internet and communication access on board (a link with the family) has become a basic component of mental health; since 2022 some flags and CBAs have made reasonable internet access a standard. The Master supports the reasonable use of the right to shore leave; preventing shore leave other than for ISPS or operational restrictions is a breach of welfare.
Zihinsel sağlık ve denizci intiharı, sek: Mental health and seafarer suicide are serious issues for the industry; isolation, fatigue and lack of contact with the family are the main risks. The Master observes the psychological state of the crew, creates an open communication environment and, if necessary, brings in the company's EAP (Employee Assistance Programme) or crisis line. Social security protection (health, disability, old age) is also within the scope of the MLC and usually runs through the flag state or the state of residence.
MLC, her gemide adil, etkili ve hızlı bi: The MLC requires every ship to have a fair, effective and quick on-board complaint procedure. A seafarer has the right to take a complaint first to his or her immediate superior and, if it is not resolved, step by step to the Master and, if necessary, to an authority ashore (DPA / company / flag state / port state official). The procedure is given to every seafarer in writing (together with the SEA), and victimisation of a seafarer for making a complaint is strictly prohibited.
Kaptan, şikâyetleri kayda geçirir, taraf: The Master records complaints and deals with them impartially and on time, and protects the seafarer's right to be accompanied or represented. The procedure includes the flag state's contact details and those of the port state authority; PSC checks whether the complaint procedure includes these final levels. A well-managed complaint procedure prevents small problems from turning into a major crisis (ITF intervention, PSC detention).
Gemide disiplin, keyfi değil belgeli ve: Discipline on board follows a documented and fair process, not an arbitrary one. The Master applies warnings, records, the sanctions defined in the SEA/CBA and, in serious cases, repatriation or termination procedures in proportion. The seafarer's right of defence, a written record of the process and witness statements are important. Excessive or arbitrary discipline is both a violation of the MLC and a source of later employment law claims.
Alkol/uyuşturucu politikası (drug & alco: The drug and alcohol policy is safety-critical and is usually based on zero tolerance or a low limit (e.g. 0.05 BAC or lower); a breach calls for serious disciplinary action. The Master carries out random and for-cause tests in accordance with the SMS, with confidentiality and respect for dignity. Keeping the line between discipline and bullying is the Master's leadership responsibility.
MLC ve ILO ilkeleri; ırk, renk, cinsiyet: MLC and ILO principles prohibit discrimination based on race, colour, sex, religion, political opinion, or national or social origin. Guidance developed since 2016 (the ICS/ITF Guidance on Eliminating Shipboard Harassment and Bullying) deals explicitly with preventing harassment and bullying on board. In multinational crews, cultural sensitivity, discipline in the use of a common (working) language and equal treatment are part of the Master's daily management.
Kaptan, taciz/zorbalık iddialarını ciddi: The Master takes allegations of harassment or bullying seriously and investigates them confidentially and fairly, protecting the victim and preventing retaliation. With the growing number of women seafarers, sexual harassment and a safe environment have come to the fore; many companies now provide a clear zero-tolerance policy and reporting channels (including off-ship and anonymous lines). Good welfare management means creating a safe climate in which problems are not hidden.
PSC denetçisi MLC açısından 14 başlığı k: For the MLC, a PSC inspector checks 14 areas: minimum age, medical certificates, seafarers' qualifications, the SEA, licensed recruitment, hours of work and rest, manning levels, accommodation, recreational facilities, food and catering, health and safety and accident prevention, on-board medical care, the on-board complaint procedure, and payment of wages. If there are "clear grounds" (a seafarer's complaint, a visible violation, an invalid document), a more detailed inspection is carried out. Inconsistent rest hour records, unpaid wages and invalid SEAs are the violations found most often.
Kaptan, denetim öncesi kendi MLC dosyası: Before an inspection the Master keeps his or her own MLC file ready (certificate, DMLC Parts I and II, sample SEAs, rest hour records, payroll, accommodation inspection records, complaint procedure). Consistent and honest records speed up the inspection; contradictory or incomplete records create a risk of detention. Findings that can be corrected are closed in port; serious or repeated violations get the ship detained.
Under the MLC, the Master's defence is the "record". Rest hour sheets are kept daily and confirmed by the seafarer; when back-filling is detected, the reliability of all the records collapses. Accommodation inspections, water tests, the medicine chest inventory, payroll and complaint records are kept with dates and signatures. These records are evidence for PSC, the flag state and any later employment law case.
Yorgunluk, denizcilik kazalarının en yay: Fatigue is the most common human-factor root cause of maritime accidents (identified in the Exxon Valdez, the Cosco Busan and countless groundings and collisions). MSC.1/Circ.1598 (Guidelines on Fatigue) deals with factors such as sleep debt, circadian rhythm, monotony and workload. The Master's most critical responsibility is to close the gap between rest hours "looking compliant on paper" and the seafarer "actually being rested".
Yetersiz manning (eksik personel) yorgun: Insufficient manning is a structural cause of fatigue; if the Master finds that the manning is not enough for the operation, he or she reports it to the DPA (under-manning is a safety and MLC issue). Intensive port rotations, frequent PSC/vetting inspections, drills and emergencies put pressure on rest hours; the Master plans according to this reality and, if necessary, takes the decision to slow down operations under the overriding authority.
Modern gemilerde mürettebat çoğunlukla ç: On modern ships the crew is mostly multinational and multicultural (Filipino, Indian, Ukrainian, Chinese, Indonesian and so on). The Master's welfare management covers clear communication in the common working language (usually English), respect for religious and cultural practices (menu, prayer times, holidays), equal treatment and preventing cliques and exclusion. Cultural sensitivity is a leadership skill that reduces tension on board and strengthens the safety culture.
Dil bariyeri, emniyet brifinglerinde ve: A language barrier is a serious risk in safety briefings and in an emergency; the Master confirms that critical instructions are understood by everyone and, if necessary, uses visual or multilingual material. Welfare and safety feed each other in a multinational team: a crew that feels valued works more safely.
MLC 2006, kaptanın \"iyi niyetle\" değil: MLC 2006 is an area in which the Master must manage "with documents", not "in good faith": every right, from the rest hour record to the payroll, from the accommodation inspection to the complaint procedure, must be visible through a record. But the real spirit of the MLC lies not on paper but in the people on board; keeping compliant records while creating a crew that feels tired, unpaid and undervalued both defeats the purpose of the MLC and sooner or later turns into a safety accident. A sensible Master knows that by protecting the crew's rights he or she is also making the strongest investment in safety: a crew that is rested, paid, healthy and treated with dignity is the most reliable line of defence at sea.
Sea protest, geminin uğradığı veya yol a: A sea protest is a formal declaration that, in damage suffered or possibly caused by the ship, the circumstances (e.g. a storm, force majeure) were beyond the control of the ship and crew. It provides an early basis of evidence against compensation claims that may be made later and protects the ship's position.
Ağır hava ve yük hasarı, çatışma, karaya: Situations such as heavy weather and cargo damage, collision, grounding, damage to shore installations or the berth, dragging anchor, unexpected delay or a dispute over cargo discharge may require a protest. When in doubt, noting a protest on the advice of the P&I Club or the company is the safe course.
Protest, genellikle limana varıştan sonr: The protest is usually made before the competent authority or a notary as soon as possible after arrival in port (often within 24 hours). Delay weakens the value of the declaration. Where necessary, a protest can be noted before the full extent of the damage is known, with the words "with reservation to extend", and extended later.
Protest, deck/official log book kayıtlar: The protest is based on the deck and official log book entries, weather data (barometer, wind, sea state), navigation records and, where necessary, witness statements. The Master documents clearly the timeline of the event, the measures taken and the conditions.
Protest metni, log ve diğer kayıtlarla b: The text of the protest must match the log and other records exactly. A contradiction damages the credibility of both the protest and the ship in general. The declaration is therefore prepared carefully on the basis of the records.
Olay sonrası P&I Club (sorumluluk sigort: After an incident the P&I Club (liability insurer) and, where necessary, the H&M underwriters are informed as soon as possible. The Club gives guidance on appointing a surveyor, legal representation and the protest strategy. The Master acts in coordination with the Club's correspondent.
Geminin ve yükün ortak kurtarılması için: If a deliberate sacrifice was made for the common safety of the ship and cargo (general average), the process runs under the York-Antwerp Rules and the protest contributes to the chain of evidence. In situations such as salvage and towage, the protest and records are also of critical importance.
Sea protest, noter/makam huzurunda yapıl: A sea protest is a formal declaration made before a notary or an authority. A Letter of Protest (LOP) is a letter given to the terminal, charterer or other party objecting to a particular situation (slow loading, damaged cargo, a dispute over measurements). The Master does not confuse the two and uses each of them in the right place and at the right time.
Deniz protestu, krizin sıcak anında gele: A sea protest is a quiet measure that, in the heat of a crisis, secures the legal position for the future. The Master's timely protest, consistent with the records, and fast coordination with the P&I Club protect the ship and crew against unjust liabilities.
B/L üç temel işlev taşır: (1) yükün beli: The B/L has three basic functions: (1) a receipt showing that the cargo was received in the stated condition and quantity, (2) evidence of the contract of carriage, (3) a negotiable document of title representing delivery of the goods. These three functions make the declaration of the Master who signs the B/L extremely binding.
Kaptan, B/L imzalanmadan önce yükün mikt: Before the B/L is signed, the Master has the quantity and apparent condition of the cargo checked against the documents. The Chief Officer's and tally records, draft survey or ullage measurements and the Mate's Receipt are the basis of this verification. If there is visible damage, a shortage or a discrepancy, the B/L is claused (a remark is added).
Görünür kusur yoksa \"clean\" B/L imzala: If there is no visible defect, a clean B/L is signed. If there is a defect, the actual condition is documented by writing it on the B/L (claused/dirty). Pressure to show damaged cargo as clean is a serious legal and ethical trap.
Mate's Receipt, yükün gemiye fiilen alın: The Mate's Receipt is the internal record documenting that the cargo was actually received on board and its condition; the B/L is issued on the basis of this receipt. The remarks (damage notes) on the Mate's Receipt must be carried over to the B/L. The Master checks that this chain is consistent.
Kaptan; Notice of Readiness (NOR — gemin: The Master approves or authorises the Notice of Readiness (NOR — notice that the ship is ready to load or discharge, which starts laytime), the Statement of Facts (SOF — the timeline of operations), the cargo manifest and the related customs documents. These documents are evidence in demurrage and commercial disputes.
Bazı durumlarda B/L'yi acente \"for and: In some cases the agent signs the B/L "for and on behalf of the Master"; this authority may be used only with the approval of the Master/company and within the instructions given. The Master is responsible for the accuracy of documents signed on his or her behalf.
B/L'de tarih değiştirme (ante/post-datin: Changing the date on a B/L (ante- or post-dating), a false statement of quantity or condition, or issuing a forged document has serious legal consequences and can invalidate insurance cover. Despite commercial pressure, the Master signs only documents that reflect the truth.
Bill of Lading, kaptanın imzasının doğru: The bill of lading is the weightiest commercial document in which the Master's signature binds the company directly. An honest signature, given only after verifying the cargo, clausing the truth and without giving in to pressure, protects both the commercial and the legal safety of the ship.
ISM Code, şirketten emniyetli işletim iç: The ISM Code requires the company to establish "safe practices" and a "safe working environment" for safe operation (section 1.2.2). A person under the influence of drugs or alcohol is a direct danger both to himself or herself and to the ship; for this reason almost every company's SMS contains a separate drug and alcohol policy. The Master is the "person in charge" responsible for actually applying this policy on board; under ISM section 5 the Master is required to implement the SMS on board and report deviations to the DPA.
Politika tipik olarak \"zero tolerance\": The policy is typically built on the principle of zero tolerance: possessing or using drugs on board, or working under their influence, is strictly prohibited and usually results in summary dismissal. For alcohol, most modern companies apply a "dry ship" policy (completely dry, 0.00 BAC) or an upper limit in line with OCIMF recommendations. The Master confirms that every new crew member joining the ship has read and signed the policy (familiarisation).
STCW 2010 Manila değişiklikleri, vardiya: The 2010 Manila amendments to STCW clearly regulate that personnel keeping a watch must be "fit for duty". Section B-VIII/1 recommends that administrations and companies set an alcohol limit and suggests 0.05% (0.5 g/L) blood alcohol concentration (BAC) or 0.25 mg/L alcohol in the breath; a lower limit is expected for some duties. Many commercial operators tighten this further, applying 0.04% (the OCIMF upper limit) or 0.00% on board.
STCW ayrıca alkol ve uyuşturucu kötüye k: STCW also considers the prevention of alcohol and drug abuse together with fatigue management under the heading of fitness for duty. A typical rule for alcohol before a watch is a window of at least 4 hours of abstinence before the start of the watch; but under dry ship policies this is not even a matter of discussion, because alcohol is prohibited on board.
D&A politikası yalnızca alkolü değil; ba: The D&A policy covers not only alcohol but also, in particular, cannabis (THC), cocaine, amphetamines/methamphetamine, opiates (morphine, codeine, heroin), benzodiazepines and synthetic substances (NPS — new psychoactive substances). Prescription medicines are not excluded: personnel using prescription medicines that may affect performance, alertness or judgement must declare this to the Master and the ship's doctor or the company's medical department. The declaration is recorded and, if necessary, duty restrictions are applied.
Politikanın kapsamı tüm mürettebat, kapt: The policy covers the whole crew, every rank including the Master, and also contractors, repair technicians and riding squads who come on board. The Master is not exempt from the zero-tolerance policy; the principle of leading by example requires the Master to be both the person who enforces the policy and the person who complies with it.
Dry ship politikası uygulayan şirketlerd: In companies with a dry ship policy, bringing alcohol on board, possessing it and consuming it are prohibited; there is no alcohol in the bond store, or it is kept locked and sealed. The Master has the authority defined in the SMS for periodic searches of cabins and common areas; these searches are made with respect for privacy, preferably in the presence of the person concerned and a witness.
Sınırlı alkole izin veren şirketlerde (ö: In companies that allow limited alcohol (e.g. on certain days, in controlled amounts), the Master keeps a record of the alcohol stock and may prohibit consumption entirely during critical port and navigation periods (manoeuvring, narrow passages, cargo operations). In every case the basic rule is that alcohol must not affect performance on watch; in case of doubt the Master may require a test (for-cause testing).
Pre-employment test, personel gemiye kat: The pre-employment test is carried out before the person joins the ship (usually by the manning agency or a clinic), and a negative result is a condition of signing on. The sign-on (joining) test is carried out when joining or shortly after, and provides a "clean start". The Master verifies that every new crew member arrives with a valid, negative D&A test certificate; if there is no certificate or it is doubtful, a test is carried out on board.
Bu testler genellikle idrar (urine) bazl: These tests are usually carried out with urine-based multi-panel immunoassay test kits, which are kept on board. If a presumptive positive result is obtained, the sample is sealed and sent for confirmation to an accredited laboratory (GC-MS/LC-MS method). The result of the screening test alone is not conclusive; the chain of custody and laboratory confirmation are therefore critical.
Random testing, programın caydırıcılığın: Random testing is the heart of the programme's deterrent effect, because no one can know in advance when they will be tested. The company SMS usually sets an annual target rate (e.g. at least 25% of the crew randomly tested once a year; some tanker companies require a higher rate). The Master ensures that the selection process is truly random and unbiased — for example a numbered list and random numbers, drawing sealed capsules, or selection by the company's central software.
Random test \"unannounced\" (habersiz) o: A random test must be unannounced; the person selected must not be given a long time between notification and giving the sample (generally sampling starts immediately). The Master records the test date and the selection method; evidence of the random programme (records, selection method, results) may be asked for in PSC or vetting inspections.
For-cause (reasonable suspicion / for-ca: A for-cause (reasonable suspicion) test is applied when a person's behaviour, speech, smell or performance gives rise to reasonable suspicion. Where possible, the observations giving rise to the suspicion are recorded by two people (the Master and an officer); not a subjective "I don't like it" but concrete signs (unsteady walk, slurred speech, smell of alcohol, bloodshot eyes) are written down. Refusing a for-cause test has the same disciplinary consequence as a positive result under most SMSs.
Post-incident (serious marine incident s: Post-incident testing (after a serious marine incident) is applied to the persons involved after events such as a collision, grounding, fire, serious injury or death, or significant pollution. In USCG waters, under 46 CFR 4.06, after a serious marine incident the alcohol test must be carried out within 2 hours and the drug test within 32 hours; missing these time windows is a separate violation. The Master plans the logistics of post-incident testing (test kits, witnesses, records) in advance as part of emergency management.
MLC, ücretin düzenli (en az ayda bir) ve: The MLC guarantees that wages are paid regularly (at least monthly) and in full; the seafarer is given a monthly wage statement (payslip) and is able to send money to his or her family (allotment). The Master monitors that wage payments on board are made in accordance with the SEA/CBA, on time and with documents; late payment is the most concrete and quickest cause of complaint for a seafarer.
Kaptan, kendi \"Master's Review\" (ISM): The Master includes MLC compliance in his or her own Master's Review (ISM) process and reports the deficiencies found and the corrective actions to the DPA. The MLC becomes sustainable when it is managed together with the ISM; keeping the two systems apart creates duplicate records and gaps.
Alkol testi gemide genellikle kalibre ed: On board, the alcohol test is usually carried out with a calibrated breathalyser (breath alcohol meter). The calibration date of the device must be valid and the calibration interval stated by the manufacturer (typically 6–12 months) must be followed. Before the test the person is expected not to have put anything in his or her mouth for at least 15–20 minutes (to prevent contamination by mouth alcohol or food); if the result is positive, a second measurement is taken after a short wait.
Sonuç ekran değeri olarak kaydedilir ve: The result is recorded as the displayed value and shown to the person tested. The Master keeps a form containing the serial number of the device, the calibration date, the time of the measurement and the result. Since breathalyser results are instant evidence that cannot be repeated later, the maintenance of the device and the stock of spare (single-use) mouthpieces are the Master's responsibility.
Uyuşturucu testi gemide multi-panel idra: On board, the drug test starts with a multi-panel urine test kit (presumptive screen). The kit shows the presence of substances above certain cut-off values. A sample that gives a presumptive positive is sealed on the split-sample principle and confirmed by GC-MS or LC-MS/MS in an accredited laboratory. Only a result confirmed by the laboratory ("confirmed positive") is accepted as a definite positive.
Cut-off değerleri madde başına farklıdır: Cut-off values differ for each substance and are based on SAMHSA and international standards as a reference. For example, roughly: amphetamines ~500 ng/mL (confirmation 250), cocaine metabolite ~150 ng/mL (confirmation 100), opiates ~2000 ng/mL, cannabis (THC-COOH) ~50 ng/mL (confirmation 15), phencyclidine ~25 ng/mL. These values are set to distinguish between environmental or passive exposure and real use; for this reason, "I was exposed by accident" defences are generally refuted by the cut-off logic.
Chain of custody (CoC), örneğin alınması: The chain of custody (CoC) is the chain in which every point of contact, from taking the sample to the laboratory result, is recorded, and it is the basis of the legal validity of the test. The sample is collected in the presence of the person tested; for a urine sample a temperature check (32–38 °C) is made to prevent substitution and dilution. The sample is sealed, the person and a witness sign the seal, and the CoC form travels with the sample.
CoC'deki bir kopukluk (mühürsüz örnek, e: A break in the CoC (an unsealed sample, a missing signature, storage that cannot be traced) makes a positive result legally indefensible. For this reason the Master takes the sample with an impartial witness and fills in every field of the form completely. If samples have to be held on board, they are kept locked and under suitable temperature conditions, and sent by courier to the laboratory at the first suitable port.
Doğrulanmış pozitif sonuçta kaptanın ilk: With a confirmed positive result, the Master's first priority is safety: the person concerned is removed at once from safety-critical duties (watchkeeping, manoeuvring, cargo operations). The company (DPA / crewing or HR department) is then notified at once; most SMSs classify a positive result as a "non-conformity / reportable event". The decision process is not left to the Master alone; the company's disciplinary procedure and legal department come in.
Çoğu zero-tolerance politikasında doğrul: Under most zero-tolerance policies, a confirmed positive results in summary dismissal and sign-off at the first suitable port. Repatriation is governed by the MLC; however, the contract and the policy may provide that in the case of a positive result the repatriation costs can be recovered from the seafarer. The Master makes sure that the whole process is documented and that the seafarer's rights (for example, the right to ask for a confirmation test) are not breached.
D&A test sonuçları hassas kişisel ve tıb: D&A test results are sensitive personal and medical data; the principle of confidentiality is followed. Results are not shared beyond those who "need to know" (the Master, the person concerned, the company official); gossip and stigmatisation on board are prevented. The Master is responsible for the process being run impartially and with respect for human dignity; behaving otherwise is contrary both to the MLC's expectation of "fair treatment" and creates legal risk.
Adil süreç (due process), pozitif sonucu: Due process means that a positive result is not applied as an automatic conviction but together with the right to confirmation and review. MRO review, the declaration of prescription medicines and the possibility of retesting with the split sample are parts of this process. The Master files every step (observation, test, result, removal from duty, notification, sign-off) time-stamped and signed; this file is decisive in any later employment law dispute.
USCG, kendi sularında 46 CFR Part 16 (ch: In its own waters the USCG inspects D&A programmes under 46 CFR Part 16 (chemical testing) and 33 CFR Part 95 (alcohol), and when necessary boards the ship to examine the testing and the programme. On US-flagged ships or ships operating in US waters, the marine employer's programme, its random testing rates and its records can be decisive. In a USCG inspection, gaps in the programme records can result in a serious finding and operational control.
Paris MOU ve diğer MOU rejimlerinde D&A: Under the Paris MOU and the other MOU regimes, D&A is not a separate inspection area as such, but it is assessed indirectly under fitness for duty, rest hours and ISM implementation. The PSC officer wants to see a D&A policy in force on board, familiarisation records and test records. If "clear grounds" arise, a more detailed inspection can be carried out.
Tanker sektöründe OCIMF SIRE/VIQ denetim: In the tanker sector, OCIMF SIRE/VIQ inspections question the D&A programme in detail: is there a written policy, are limit values defined, is the random testing rate sufficient, are records kept, is the breathalyser calibrated? In vetting, a weak D&A programme directly affects the ship's acceptability for charter; this requires the Master to run the programme rigorously not only for "compliance" but also for commercial sustainability.
Kaptan, vetting öncesi bir iç denetimle: Before vetting, the Master closes the gaps in the programme with an internal audit (self-assessment): an expired calibration, missing familiarisation signatures and unrecorded random tests are the most common findings. This preparation considerably reduces the stress of the inspection day and the number of observations.
Etkili bir D&A politikası yalnızca test: An effective D&A policy is not only testing and punishment; it also covers prevention and training. At periodic safety meetings the Master explains the D&A risks, the scope of the policy and how testing works. When the crew see the policy not as a "trap to catch people" but as a framework that protects everyone's safety, voluntary acceptance of the programme increases.
MLC 2006'nın mürettebat refahı (welfare): The emphasis of MLC 2006 on crew welfare encourages treating alcohol and drug dependence as a health problem as well as a disciplinary one. Some companies offer "self-referral" (asking for help voluntarily): if a seafarer asks for help before a positive test, he or she is referred to rehabilitation. The Master supports the existence and the confidentiality of such a channel.
Gemide uzun seferler, izolasyon, monoton: Long voyages, isolation, monotony and fatigue on board are factors that increase the risk of escaping into alcohol or drugs. The Master takes indirect measures by managing these environmental risks (social activities, means of communication, reasonable rest).
