The D&A policy and fatigue management (rest hours) complement each other; both are part of fitness for duty.
İçki sorunu olan bir personelin tespiti: A seafarer with a drinking problem is usually identified not suddenly but through gradual signs (lateness, falling performance, social withdrawal). The Master's ability to observe allows the problem to be caught early, before a for-cause test. Early intervention is the most effective defence for the safety of both the person and the ship.
Kaptan, D&A programının tüm ayak izini k: The Master keeps a record of the whole footprint of the D&A programme: signed policy and familiarisation forms, the random test selection method and results, observation reports for for-cause and post-incident tests, breathalyser calibration documents, records of test kit stock and expiry dates, and correspondence on positive results. These records must be ready both for internal audits and for PSC and vetting.
Kayıtların gizliliği ve saklama süresi ş: The confidentiality and retention period of the records follow the company procedure; since they are personal data, access is restricted. Summaries of results (how many tests, how many positives) can be reported in anonymised form; individual results, however, are shared only with authorised persons.
Pozitif sonuç, for-cause test kararı vey: A positive result, a decision to carry out a for-cause test or a breach of the policy is reported to the DPA on time under the ISM. The report contains a summary of the event, the immediate measure taken (removal from duty), the test details and the recommended action. The DPA and the company's HR and legal departments coordinate the logistics of sign-off and repatriation, the provision of a relief and the legal steps.
Kaptan, bu sürecin \"tek karar verici\": The Master knows that in this process he or she is not the "sole decision-maker" but the "manager on site and the one who reports". The safety decision (removal from duty) belongs to the Master at once; but termination of employment and legal representation are handled together with the company. This clarity both protects the Master and ensures that the seafarer's rights are protected.
D&A politikasının uygulanmasında kaptanı: The Master's success in applying the D&A policy is not that "there are never any positives" but that the programme runs consistently, impartially, with documents and with respect for human dignity. Zero tolerance is a strong deterrent; but its strength comes from the legal soundness of its application and from the crew's trust in this framework. A well-managed D&A programme is the invisible line of defence that will one day prevent an accident; a badly managed programme leaves both safety and the company legally exposed.
H&M poliçesi, geminin kendi gövdesine ve: The H&M policy is a property insurance covering physical damage to the ship's own hull and machinery (hull and machinery damage). It is typically built on standard sets of clauses such as the Institute Time Clauses (Hulls). Deformation of the hull caused by a collision, fire damage in the engine room, bottom plating damage after a grounding, or propeller or shaft damage are covered by H&M. Through the "running down clause" (RDC / 3/4ths collision liability), H&M can also cover a certain proportion of the damage caused to the other ship in a collision.
H&M poliçesinde bir muafiyet (deductible: An H&M policy has a deductible; small damage that stays below this deductible is borne by the ship or the company. The "sue and labour" clause (Marine Insurance Act 1906) provides for the assured to incur reasonable expenses to reduce the loss and for these expenses to be met by the insurer — the Master's efforts to limit the damage after an incident are important in this respect.
P&I, geminin üçüncü taraflara karşı soru: P&I is a system of mutual insurance covering the ship's third-party liabilities; it works through clubs formed by shipowners. P&I cover typically includes: liability for cargo damage or loss, injury or death of crew and third parties, pollution (oil pollution) liability, wreck removal, the 1/4 collision liability not covered by H&M, port and dock damage, fines, and expenses such as stowaways and repatriation.
Birçok kulüp, ayrıca FD&D (Freight, Demu: Many clubs also offer FD&D (Freight, Demurrage & Defence) protection as a separate cover; it meets legal costs in contractual disputes (charter party, freight, demurrage). The Master's practical task is to assess quickly whether an incident concerns H&M, P&I or both, and to inform both channels in time; because a collision can at the same time cause damage to his or her own ship (H&M), liability towards the other party (P&I) and a cargo claim (P&I).
P&I kulüp kuralları ve H&M poliçeleri, s: P&I club rules and H&M policies require the assured to report an incident "without undue delay". Late notification can weaken cover to the extent that the club or the insurer suffers prejudice. As soon as an incident occurs, the Master informs the company (DPA / operations); the company in turn formally notifies the H&M and P&I insurers. Many companies keep an emergency contact list from which the Master can call the P&I correspondent directly.
Bildirim, soğukkanlı ve olgusal olmalıdı: The report must be calm and factual. The Master avoids statements admitting liability ("we made a mistake"), because early and unconsidered admissions later become evidence against the ship. The report contains the place and time (UTC) of the incident, the weather and visibility conditions, the condition of the ship, whether there are injured or dead persons or pollution, and the immediate measures taken.
Kaptan, olaydan hemen sonra delilleri si: Immediately after an incident the Master systematically preserves and collects the evidence: deck and engine log book entries (time-stamped and true), the bell book / movement book, ECDIS and radar records, the data of the VDR (Voyage Data Recorder) saved and preserved, the GMDSS log, weather reports, photographs and video, and the crew's notes as witnesses. If the VDR record is not saved immediately after the incident, it can be overwritten and lost; securing the VDR is therefore a priority of the first minutes.
Kargo, kirlilik veya yaralanma içeren ol: In incidents involving cargo, pollution or injury, the scene is preserved as far as possible until the surveyor arrives. The Master takes photographs of the damaged areas, records the measurements (soundings, draft, ullage) and gathers all the documents in a single "casualty file". This file is the basic source for any later P&I claim, the GA adjustment and court proceedings.
Bir olayın ardından birden çok surveyor: After an incident several surveyors may come on board, and each has a different principal. The H&M underwriter appoints its own surveyor (to establish hull and machinery damage); the P&I club appoints its own surveyor (for liability and cargo); the other party (for example the ship that was struck, or the cargo interests) may send its own surveyor; and the class society assesses the class status (condition of class). The Master must know which surveyor represents whom and adjust the level of cooperation accordingly.
Kendi sigortacı/kulüp surveyor'larıyla t: Full cooperation is given to the surveyors of the ship's own insurer and club. Reasonable access is given to the other party's surveyor, but statements and documents are shared under the direction of the company and the P&I club; giving uncontrolled statements to the other party's surveyor can create evidence against the ship. The Master records every surveyor visit: whom the surveyor represents, what was examined and what was documented.
Hasar tespit raporları (survey reports),: Survey reports are the basis of compensation and of the apportionment of liability. The Master also documents independently the extent and nature of the damage observed by the surveyor; consistency is sought between the surveyor's report and the ship's own records. Whether the damage was "pre-existing" or caused by this incident is often disputed; for this reason the ship's regular maintenance and class records (to prove the condition before the damage) are critical.
Kargo hasarında, hasarın gemiye yüklenme: In cargo damage, distinguishing whether the damage occurred before the cargo was loaded (clausing / a remark on the Mate's Receipt) or during carriage determines liability for compensation. The Master documents observations of damage during loading and discharging with a Letter of Protest and a survey. These records are used directly in the P&I club's defence of the cargo claim.
Gemi tehlikedeyse (oturmuş, yangın, maki: If the ship is in danger (aground, on fire, drifting with an engine failure) and outside salvage assistance is needed, the most common contract is Lloyd's Open Form (LOF). LOF is based on the "no cure – no pay" principle: if the salvor succeeds, it receives an award; if it fails, nothing is paid. The great advantage of LOF is that it can be signed quickly at a moment of danger without lengthy price negotiations; the amount of the award is determined afterwards by Lloyd's arbitration.
Kaptan, tehlike (peril) durumunda LOF im: In a situation of peril the Master has the authority to sign LOF; but where possible he or she first contacts the company and the P&I and H&M insurers. If time is critical and there is no communication, the Master signs LOF for the safety of the ship and crew — this authority is supported by the priority given to safety in SOLAS and by maritime custom. After signing, the company and the insurers are informed at once.
SCOPIC (Special Compensation P&I Clause): SCOPIC (Special Compensation P&I Clause) is a mechanism that can be added to LOF and comes into play especially in salvage operations involving an environmental risk. Under the classic "no cure – no pay" logic, a salvor can make a loss when salving a ship that threatens the environment but has a low commercial value; SCOPIC pays the salvor reasonable expenses plus a certain margin regardless of success. SCOPIC compensation is typically paid by the P&I club.
SCOPIC devreye alındığında, P&I'ın atadı: When SCOPIC is invoked, an SCR (Special Casualty Representative) appointed on behalf of the P&I side joins the operation and monitors the salvage expenses. The Master works in coordination with the SCR and the salvage master; the ship's crew usually give practical support to the salvage operation (for example the towing connection, pumping, damage control). Throughout, safety and protection of the environment have priority.
Her dış yardım salvage değildir. Gemi ac: Not all outside assistance is salvage. If the ship is not in immediate danger but needs assistance (for example being towed to port after an engine failure, a dead tow), this is carried out under a towage contract. BIMCO's standard contracts Towcon (lump sum) and Towhire (daily hire) are used for this purpose. The distinction between salvage and towage is important, because a salvage award can be much higher than a towage fee.
Kaptan, durumu doğru sınıflandırır: gerç: The Master classifies the situation correctly: if there is no real peril and negotiation is possible, a towage contract is preferred because it has a known and fixed cost. However, if the situation deteriorates during a towage operation and a real peril arises, it can turn into salvage. The Master coordinates the type of contract and the basis of payment with the company and the P&I club.
General Average (GA), örneğin yangını sö: General Average (GA) is the sharing of sacrifices made to escape a common danger, such as cargo being damaged by water to put out a fire, cargo being thrown overboard (jettison) to refloat a grounded ship, or salvage and towage expenses. When GA is declared, the contribution of all the parties saved (the shipowner and all the cargo owners) to the losses is calculated under the York-Antwerp Rules (commonly the 2016 version).
GA'yı ilan etme kararı genelde gemi sahi: The decision to declare GA is generally taken by the shipowner or the company, which appoints an average adjuster; however, the Master is responsible for documenting completely all the details of the event giving rise to GA (jettison, firefighting, salvage). The Master's records (which cargo was sacrificed, when and on what grounds) are the basis of the GA adjustment.
GA ilan edildiğinde, kargo sahiplerinden: When GA is declared, documents securing their contributions are required from the cargo owners: an Average Bond (an undertaking signed by the cargo owner) and an Average Guarantee (a guarantee given by the cargo's insurer), or a cash deposit. Cargo is not delivered until this security is complete, because once the cargo has been delivered it becomes very difficult to collect the contribution. This process often delays delivery and requires careful coordination.
Average adjuster (örneğin Richards Hogg: The average adjuster (firms such as Richards Hogg Lindley, for example) draws up the "general average statement", which determines each party's contribution by calculating the value of all the interests saved and the amount of the sacrifices. This process can take months or years. The Master's task is to give the adjuster accurate and complete documents; missing documents both delay the adjustment and can lead to items in the shipowner's favour not being admitted to GA.
Kaptan, gemi ve şirket adına hukuki süre: The Master is the primary point of contact on site for legal proceedings on behalf of the ship and the company. After an incident, notices from courts or authorities (writ, arrest warrant, subpoena), requests for investigation from the port or coastal state and legal correspondence from the other party reach the Master first. Before signing or replying to these documents, the Master always contacts the company and the FD&D or legal department of the P&I club. A hasty signature or statement can weaken the ship's legal position.
Sworn statement (yeminli ifade), affidav: A sworn statement, an affidavit or statements in an investigation directly affect the legal outcome of an incident. The Master takes legal advice before giving a statement; the statement must be based on facts, consistent and in line with the ship's records. Relying on the records instead of saying "I don't recall", not contradicting oneself and avoiding speculation are the basic principles.
Sea Protest (Note of Protest), kaptanın: A Sea Protest (Note of Protest) is a declaration by which the Master formally records, after an unusual event (heavy weather, grounding, risk of cargo damage, collision), that he or she and the ship were not at fault and that the damage was caused by external factors. It is made before a notary or a consul at the first suitable port, generally within a reasonable time after arrival (often within 24 hours). A Sea Protest strengthens the ship's position against later cargo claims and GA proceedings.
Kaptan, Sea Protest'i \"extended\" (geni: The Master can also prepare the Sea Protest as "extended", which reserves the right to submit further evidence later. A Sea Protest does not remove liability by itself; but as a formal and timely declaration it records the ship's good faith and the facts. The Master applies protest practice under the direction of the company and the P&I club.
Her büyük limanda P&I kulübünün bir corr: In every major port the P&I club has a correspondent (local representative). The correspondent is like the Master's eyes, ears and hands in that port: arranges surveyors, engages local lawyers, negotiates security, handles communication with the authorities and collects the necessary documents. When an incident occurs, one of the Master's first calls (with the company's approval) should be to the P&I correspondent in that port; the correspondent list is kept up to date on board.
Correspondent ile çalışırken kaptan, olg: When working with the correspondent, the Master is factual and transparent; however, the legal strategy and the assessment of liability are directed by the correspondent and the club's lawyers. The Master meets the correspondent's requests (documents, statements, access) in coordination with the company. This cooperation keeps the process both quick and legally protected.
Bir ciddi olay, eş zamanlı olarak birçok: A serious incident sets many parties in motion at the same time: the company (DPA / operations), the H&M and P&I insurers, the class society (condition of class), the flag state and, where necessary, the coastal state (accident investigation, pollution authority). ISM Code section 9 requires non-conformities and accidents to be reported to the company and analysed, with corrective action. At the centre of this multi-party communication, the Master presents one consistent, factual account.
Koordinasyonun anahtarı, tek bir \"casua: The key to coordination is a single "casualty file" and a single set of facts: telling different stories to different parties is a disaster. The Master records all correspondence and tracks who asked for what and what was shared. This discipline both speeds up insurance recovery and removes the risk of contradictions in legal proceedings.
Sigorta ve hukuki muhataplıkta kaptanın: In insurance and legal matters, the Master's strength comes not from taking decisions alone but from bringing in the right party at the right moment and documenting the facts flawlessly. In a marine incident, what determines the financial outcome is often not the incident itself but the quality of the evidence collected in the first hours after it and the timing of the notifications. A well-managed casualty process ensures that the ship receives the cover it deserves in full; a badly managed process can leave even a ship that was in the right uninsured and legally exposed.
Yorgunluk; tepki süresini uzatır, dikkat: Fatigue lengthens reaction time, distracts attention, impairs judgement and leads to dangerous states such as "microsleep". Fatigue plays a direct or indirect part in most accidents on the bridge and in the engine room. The Master sees fatigue not as a "weakness" but as a serious operational risk that must be managed.
Yetersiz uyku, bölünmüş dinlenme, ağır i: The main factors are insufficient sleep, broken rest, heavy workload, intensive port operations, noise and vibration, disruption of the circadian rhythm (night watches, frequent time zone changes) and stress. On ships with small crews, the intensity of port calls and manoeuvring rapidly increases fatigue.
STCW/MLC; her 24 saatte en az 10 saat ve: STCW and the MLC require at least 10 hours of rest in any 24-hour period and at least 77 hours in any 7-day period. Rest may be divided into no more than two periods, one of which must be at least 6 hours without interruption, and the interval between consecutive periods of rest must not exceed 14 hours. The Master sees to it that these limits are not breached.
Acil durum ve drill'ler için sınırlı ist: Although limited exceptions are defined for emergencies and drills, they must not be abused; compensatory rest is given after an exception. The Master avoids a crew that is "compliant on paper but tired in reality".
Rest hours kayıtları, gerçek dinlenmeyi: Rest hour records must reflect real rest. Keeping false records to show compliance (record falsification) is both a violation of the MLC and a collapse of the safety culture, because it hides real fatigue and makes the risk invisible. The Master insists on honest records.
Manevra, dar su geçişi, yoğun yük operas: Before manoeuvring, passages through narrow waters, intensive cargo operations or bad weather, the personnel concerned are made sure to be rested. The Master plans the port programme and the allocation of duties so as to reduce fatigue; if necessary, operations are slowed down or extra rest is given.
Esneme, dikkat dağınıklığı, gecikmiş tep: Yawning, distraction, delayed reactions, irritability and an increase in errors are signs of fatigue. The Master builds a culture in which the crew can report fatigue without hesitation; saying "I am tired" is not punished but taken seriously.
Yorgunluk yönetimi, kaptanın hem yasal y: Fatigue management is both the Master's legal obligation and one of the most effective tools for preventing accidents. Honest records, realistic workload planning and an open culture minimise the invisible risk that a tired crew can cause.
Bir stowaway tespit edildiğinde öncelik: When a stowaway is discovered, the priority is human safety: the person's safety of life and basic needs (water, food, shelter, medical care) are provided. At the same time, for the security of the ship, the person is kept under supervision. The Master ensures that the person is treated humanely and in accordance with the regulations; ill-treatment is unacceptable.
Kaptan; kişinin bulunma koşullarını, kim: The Master documents the circumstances in which the person was found, his or her identity details (if any), state of health and the supervision arrangements. The P&I Club is informed early (stowaway costs are covered by P&I). Disembarkation and return are carried out in coordination with the states concerned and the agent.
Yüksek riskli bölgelerde (geçmişte Aden: In high-risk areas (in the past the Gulf of Aden / Indian Ocean, the Gulf of Guinea, some South-East Asian waters), BMP is applied. The Master carries out a risk assessment and prepares the ship protection measures (physical barriers, razor wire, water spray), the speed and manoeuvring plan and the lookout arrangements. Crew awareness and drills are critical.
Saldırı durumunda mürettebatın korunaklı: In the event of an attack, the crew are planned to withdraw to a protected area (the citadel); the citadel is kept ready with communications, water and food. UKMTO/MSCHOA and the naval units concerned are informed; the SSAS (Ship Security Alert System) is activated when necessary. The safety of the crew always comes before the ship and the cargo.
ISPS Code kapsamında gemi, güvenlik sevi: Under the ISPS Code the ship applies the Ship Security Plan (SSP) according to the security level (1-2-3). The Master and the SSO arrange access control, monitoring of restricted areas, the security of cargo and stores, and the management of visitors. Changes of security level are recorded.
Hırsızlık, sabotaj, izinsiz giriş, bomb: Security incidents such as theft, sabotage, unauthorised entry, a bomb threat or a suspicious situation are managed in accordance with the SSP and reported to the company, the PFSO and the authorities. The SSAS provides a covert alarm when life or the ship is threatened. The Master carries out the recording and corrective action after the incident.
Hem stowaway hem de gözaltına alınan şüp: Humane treatment is mandatory both for stowaways and for suspects held in custody. The Master strikes the balance between the security of the ship and human rights within the framework of the regulations; excessive force, ill-treatment or putting the person in danger are unacceptable and create heavy liability.
Güvenlik olayları yönetimi, kaptanın hem: Managing security incidents is an area in which the Master uses together the composure of command, humane responsibility and knowledge of the regulations. A prepared ship — drilled, with plans, connected to the reporting network — turns these incidents not into panic but into a controlled procedure.
IHR 2005, hastalıkların uluslararası yay: IHR 2005 aims to prevent the international spread of disease without unnecessarily restricting travel and trade. Ships are at the centre of this regime: port health authorities ask the ship for a health declaration and, when necessary, carry out inspections and apply measures. The Master is responsible for the ship's compliance with this framework.
MDoH, geminin son uğraklarında ve seyir: The MDoH (Maritime Declaration of Health) is the official declaration reporting to the port authority cases of illness or death that occurred at the ship's last ports of call and during the voyage, the sanitary conditions and known health risks. The Master prepares the declaration accurately and completely; concealment or a false declaration creates serious liability.
Ship Sanitation Control Exemption Certif: The Ship Sanitation Control Exemption Certificate (SSCEC) or Ship Sanitation Control Certificate (SSCC) documents the ship's sanitary conditions and its pest and rodent control; it is generally valid for 6 months and is renewed at authorised ports. The Master follows the validity of the certificate and plans the port of renewal; an expired certificate causes problems in port.
Bir mürettebatta bulaşıcı hastalık şüphe: When a communicable disease is suspected in a crew member, the patient is isolated, hygiene and contact measures are taken, TMAS is consulted and the health authority of the port of arrival is notified under the IHR. The Master manages the risk of an outbreak transparently, without concealment; this is both for the crew and for public health.
Sağlık serbestisi (free pratique) alınan: Until free pratique is granted, the "Q" flag is hoisted when required — the ship declares that it is healthy and requests free pratique. Without the approval of the health authority (radio pratique or face-to-face pratique), persons boarding and leaving are restricted where required. The Master applies this signalling and the procedure correctly.
Belirli bölge geçişlerinde (örn. sarı hu: For passages through certain regions (e.g. areas where yellow fever is endemic), vaccination and a valid vaccination certificate may be required. The Master follows the vaccination status of the crew. General hygiene, drinking water quality, food safety and pest control are the basic measures that prevent disease in the first place.
Gemi sağlık prosedürleri, mürettebatı ve: Ship health procedures are an invisible shield that protects the crew and the communities visited from communicable diseases. The Master's up-to-date documents, transparent declarations and sound sanitation discipline ensure both legal compliance and real public health safety.
Acil durum komuta yapısı tipik olarak üç: The emergency command structure is typically built around three centres: the bridge (command centre — the Master in command, overall coordination, navigation and communications), the scene of the incident (on-scene command — generally the Chief Officer, who directs the response teams) and the engine control room (the Chief Engineer — management of the engines, fire pumps, generators, steering gear and emergency power). The Master is not the person who runs to the scene, but the one who sees the whole picture, manages the resources and handles external communication. This separation prevents the mistake of "the Master getting lost at the scene".
Müster listesi (muster list — SOLAS III/: The muster list (SOLAS III/8) shows each crew member's duty in an emergency, the muster station, the equipment assigned and the meaning of the alarm signals. The general emergency alarm consists of seven or more short blasts followed by one long blast. The Master continually confirms that the muster list is up to date and that each person knows his or her duty (fire party, rescue party, first aid, liferaft preparation, bridge support).
Kriz kararları çoğu zaman eksik bilgi ve: Crisis decisions are usually taken with incomplete information and under time pressure. An effective approach is the OODA loop of military origin (Observe–Orient–Decide–Act), or the GRADE model taken over from aviation: Gather (collect information), Review (review the information and the risks), Analyse (analyse the options), Decide (take the decision), Evaluate (assess the outcome). Rather than freezing while waiting for perfect information, the Master takes a "good enough" decision early and updates it as conditions change; because in a crisis the most expensive decision is no decision at all.
Kaptan, bilişsel tuzaklara (tunnel visio: The Master must be alert to cognitive traps (tunnel vision, plan continuation bias, fixation on a wrong picture of the situation). As in the El Faro case, clinging to the first plan when it is no longer valid is fatal. Keeping the "challenge and response" culture on the bridge during a crisis as well is the strongest safeguard covering the Master's blind spots; an officer being able to say "shouldn't we reconsider this?" saves lives in a crisis.
GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safe: GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safety System) is regulated by SOLAS Chapter IV and recognises three levels of priority: Distress (MAYDAY — a ship or a person is in grave and imminent danger and needs immediate assistance), Urgency (PAN-PAN — an urgent but not life-threatening situation concerning the safety of a ship or a person, e.g. a serious medical case) and Safety (SECURITE — a navigational or meteorological warning). The Master chooses the level that matches the real seriousness of the situation; a distress alert sent too late is as dangerous as an unnecessary one.
Distress mesajı önce DSC (Digital Select: The distress message is first sent by DSC (Digital Selective Calling) (VHF Ch 70, MF/HF distress frequencies), followed by a spoken MAYDAY call by radiotelephone (VHF Ch 16, MF 2182 kHz): MAYDAY ×3, the ship's name and call sign, position, nature of the distress, assistance required, number of persons on board and other information. Several channels are used: satellite (Inmarsat/Iridium) and, if necessary, the EPIRB. An accurate and up-to-date position determines how quickly rescue arrives.
EPIRB (Emergency Position Indicating Rad: The EPIRB (Emergency Position Indicating Radio Beacon) is activated automatically (hydrostatic release) when the ship sinks, or manually; it sends the ship's identity and GPS position to the Cospas-Sarsat satellites on 406 MHz. The SART (Search and Rescue Transponder) is a radar transponder used in the survival craft; it appears as a distinctive line of dots on the radar display of a searching ship. The Master writes into the muster procedure that the EPIRB and the SART are taken along when abandoning ship.
Distress aldıktan sonra koordinasyonu MR: After a distress alert is received, the MRCC (Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre) takes over coordination. The MRCC may designate an OSC (On-Scene Coordinator); this role is taken by the first ship to arrive or the most capable one, which directs the search pattern (expanding square, sector search, parallel track) in accordance with the IAMSAR Manual. The Master must know the IAMSAR procedures both when calling for help and when going to the assistance of another ship; SOLAS V/33 makes it a legal obligation to assist persons in distress.
Yangın alarmında kaptanın ilk kararları:: The Master's first decisions on a fire alarm: the location and class of the fire are established, the general alarm is sounded, the response team (generally led by the Chief Officer) is sent with equipment (SCBA, fireman's outfit, hoses), ventilation and fire dampers are checked, and the ship is manoeuvred so that the wind does not fan the fire (reducing the relative wind and keeping smoke and flames away from the accommodation and the fire party). Boundary cooling (cooling the adjacent spaces with water from outside) is the basis of preventing the fire from spreading.
Yangın sınıfına göre söndürücü seçilir:: The extinguishing agent is chosen according to the class of fire: class A (solids) water; class B (oil/fuel) foam or CO2; class C (gas) shutting off the source; electrical fires CO2 or clean agent (with the power isolated). In an engine room fire, the fixed CO2 or water mist system is used as a last resort; but before CO2 is released it must be confirmed beyond doubt that the space has been completely evacuated and a head count has been made. The Master personally obtains this "is everyone out?" confirmation.
Kaptan, müdahale ekibinin güvenliğini ya: The Master considers the safety of the response team as important as putting out the fire. The SCBA air time is monitored (BA control — the air control board), the team enters in pairs, and a withdrawal signal and a back-up team are ready. Because of the risk of re-ignition, the area continues to be watched and its temperature monitored after the fire has been extinguished. The principle is not one person's heroics but a disciplined response that can always be withdrawn.
Konteyner gemilerinde güvertedeki ve amb: Fires in container stacks on deck and in the holds (especially those caused by mis-declared DG) are very difficult: access to the stacks is limited, water may not be enough and there is a structural risk. Cases such as the Maersk Honam (2018) show that the Master sometimes cannot fully extinguish the fire and that withdrawing the team and waiting for outside help (salvage, escort) may be the right course. The Master's task is not to beat the fire at the cost of losing the team, but to protect people.
Çatışma kaçınılmaz hale geldiğinde son d: When a collision becomes unavoidable, the aim is to minimise the angle and speed of impact with a last-minute manoeuvre (COLREG Rules 8 and 17) and with the engine; if possible, the ship is manoeuvred so that the impact is taken in the bow area (the strongest structure). Immediately after a collision the Master simultaneously manages: checking for injured persons, assessing flooding, damage control, the risk of pollution and communication with the other ship. If the two ships are locked together, the decision to separate can increase flooding; this assessment is made carefully.
COLREG Rule 19 ve sınırlı görüş hükümler: COLREG Rule 19 and the provisions on restricted visibility are among the root causes of most collisions. After a collision the Master has legal obligations: to assist the other ship and the persons on board, to exchange the ship's name, port of registry and ports of departure and destination, and to record the event. SOLAS V/33 and international custom require assistance to be given to the other ship as far as this can be done without endangering one's own ship.
Su alma durumunda kaptan ve Birinci Zabi: In a flooding situation the Master and the Chief Officer use the damage stability information (the ship's damage stability booklet, subdivision plans) to assess which compartments are flooded, the ship's tendency to sink or capsize, and whether counter-flooding is needed. Closing the watertight doors, managing the bilge and ballast pumps and controlling the list are vital. Progressive flooding is the silent killer behind the sinking of many ships.
Kaptan, geminin kurtarılabilir mi yoksa: When deciding whether the ship can be saved or must be abandoned, the Master must read the time correctly: abandoning too early can cause unnecessary loss of life, abandoning too late can be fatal. The principle "the ship carries the people, not the people the ship" is the guide; but if staying on board is still safer than a liferaft (the ship being a rescue platform as long as it does not sink), the Master weighs this too.
Karaya oturma anında ilk refleks makiney: At the moment of grounding, the first reflex may be to try to get off by going astern on the engine; this is often a mistake. The Master first assesses the situation: where the ship is aground (bow, stern, full length), the type of bottom (sand, mud, rock), hull integrity, flooding, the state of the tide and the environmental risk. Going astern hastily can tear the damaged area open and multiply flooding and pollution; moreover, a damaged ship that slides off into deep water can sink.
Kaptan; tank ve bölme soundinglerini ald: The Master has the tanks and compartments sounded (to detect flooding), compares the draft readings, calculates the high-water window from the tide tables and, if necessary, prepares a refloating plan with salvage and class advice. If there is a risk of pollution, the SOPEP is activated and the authorities are informed. A controlled and calculated refloating plan, rather than hasty decisions, protects both the ship and the environment.
Karaya oturmalar büyük çevre felaketleri: Groundings can turn into major environmental disasters (Exxon Valdez 1989, Wakashio 2020). The Master gives priority to the condition of the fuel tanks; if necessary, he or she reduces the risk of pollution by internal transfer (moving cargo or fuel into intact tanks). The SOPEP/SMPEP contains the initial response equipment and the notification list. The port or coastal state, class and the P&I club are informed quickly; a surveyor is appointed.
Kaptan, olayın tüm zaman çizelgesini (lo: The Master preserves the whole timeline of the event (log, ECDIS replay, statements of the lookouts) and prepares for a formal sea protest. The lesson of the Wakashio case is clear: deviating from the passage plan for personal reasons (closing the coast) is a trigger of major accidents. Crisis management covers not only the moment of the event but also the records and the legal process afterwards.
MOB anında ilk eylemler: \"MAN OVERBOARD: First actions on a MOB: "MAN OVERBOARD" is shouted, a lifebuoy (with light and smoke signal) is thrown to the side the person fell, the MOB button is pressed (marking the GPS position), the rudder is put over to the side the person fell (to swing the propeller away from the person), and a lookout keeps the person in sight continuously and never loses sight of him or her. The Master is called to the bridge and chooses a suitable turning manoeuvre: the Williamson turn (person out of sight, returning along the same track), the Anderson turn (person in sight, quickest turn) or the Scharnow turn.
Kurtarma botu/rescue boat hazırlanır, MO: The rescue boat is prepared and launched with the procedure practised in MOB drills. Water temperature is a critical factor: in cold water hypothermia begins within minutes, so speed is vital. The Master also looks after the safety of the rescue team; to avoid further casualties, the rescue boat crew are sent with lifejackets and the necessary equipment.
Kurtarılan kişiye hipotermi ve boğulma p: The rescued person is treated according to the hypothermia and drowning protocol; the ship's medical equipment and personnel competent in first aid come in. In serious cases a shore doctor is consulted by telemedicine (e.g. TMAS — Telemedical Maritime Assistance Service) and, if necessary, a MEDEVAC (evacuation by helicopter) is requested through the MRCC. The Master runs this chain (including a PAN-PAN urgency call) quickly.
MOB olayları çoğu zaman güverte çalışmas: MOB events usually arise from preventable causes such as work on deck, seasickness or not using a safety harness. After the event the Master investigates the root cause (overboard work permit, harness use, maintenance of the guardrails) and prevents recurrence; prevention is as much a part of crisis management as rescue.
Gemiyi terk, kaptanın verebileceği en ağ: Abandoning ship is the gravest decision the Master can take and is the last resort. In line with the principle "abandon the ship when it can no longer carry you", every moment the ship stays afloat she is a safer platform than a liferaft. The Master must take the decision to abandon neither too early (abandoning a ship that could be saved) nor too late (a disorderly evacuation at the moment of sinking). When the decision is taken, the abandon ship signal is sounded and the crew assemble at the muster stations with lifejackets and immersion suits.
Tahliye, müster listesine göre düzenli y: The evacuation proceeds in an orderly way according to the muster list: the liferafts and boats are prepared and launched, the EPIRB and SART are taken, the necessary documents and water and provisions are loaded, and a head count is made. The Master leaves last and confirms that every member of the crew has been counted. Cold water, darkness and bad weather make evacuation far more difficult; this is why the equipment must be familiar and practised in drills.
Can salına/bota geçtikten sonra hayatta: Once in the liferaft or boat, survival management begins: a head count, conserving heat (rafts are tied together, openings are closed), rationing water and provisions, hydration (seawater is not drunk), managing seasickness, and morale. The Master or a senior officer continues to lead in the raft; position and visibility (flares, SART, signalling mirror) are managed. Cold is the greatest threat; hypothermia takes more lives than drowning.
Kurtarma gelene kadar düzen ve umut koru: Order and hope must be kept until rescue arrives. The Master also practises this psychological dimension in drills (managing panic, allocating tasks), because how people behave in a crisis is as decisive as the equipment. A well-drilled crew stays orderly even in bad conditions.
SOLAS III/19, fire ve abandon ship drill: SOLAS III/19 makes fire and abandon ship drills mandatory every month (weekly on passenger ships) and enclosed space entry and rescue drills at least every two months. In addition, the company SMS plans MOB, pollution (SOPEP), grounding, blackout, steering failure, helicopter operation and security drills. The Master fits the drill schedule to the voyage programme and ensures that no drill is done only "on paper".
Gerçekçi bir drill; beklenmedik bir sena: A realistic drill includes an unexpected scenario (e.g. "this exit is blocked, find another"), timing, use of real equipment and a debrief afterwards. "Went well / to be improved" notes are written in the drill records, and the gaps found are turned into corrective action. A bad drill creates false confidence, which is more dangerous than not drilling at all.
Krizde kaptan, içeride komutayı sürdürür: In a crisis the Master must keep command on board while managing accurate and timely communication with the outside. The company's Emergency Response Team (ERT) comes into action; the Master coordinates with the DPA/CSO and the company crisis line. The flow of communication is defined in advance: who calls, what information is given, who speaks to the media (generally the company, not the Master). Early, honest and regular information speeds up outside support and prevents misinformation.
Kaptan, kriz boyunca bir olay günlüğü (i: Throughout the crisis the Master keeps an incident log: time-stamped decisions, messages and changes in the situation. This record both makes operational coordination easier and is critical evidence for the subsequent investigation, insurance and legal proceedings. Memory is unreliable in a crisis; a written record is reliable.
Kriz atlatıldıktan sonra mürettebatın fi: Once the crisis is over, the physical and psychological care of the crew comes first. The injured are treated and a MEDEVAC is arranged if necessary. Post-traumatic stress (losing a crew member, having been in danger of death) can leave serious effects; the Master arranges a debriefing and, if necessary, professional support (psychological first aid, counselling ashore). People are at the centre of the crisis and remain so after the event is over.
Kaptan, mürettebatın dinlenme ve toparla: The Master looks after the crew's need for rest and recovery (including MLC rest hours). Returning to normal operations with an exhausted team after a crisis invites new errors; if necessary, additional personnel or port support is requested.
Olay, ISM madde 9 kapsamında raporlanır: The event is reported under ISM section 9 and a root cause analysis is carried out. The VDR (Voyage Data Recorder) data is preserved (the recording is saved or backed up so that it is not overwritten), and the logs, ECDIS replay and statements are archived. The Master gives honest and complete information to the flag state's casualty investigation (Casualty Investigation Code), to the P&I/H&M process and, if necessary, to judicial proceedings.
Her ciddi olay, filo için bir öğrenme fı: Every serious incident is a learning opportunity for the fleet. Corrective actions are applied not only on that ship but throughout the company. A modern safety culture focuses not on "whom shall we blame" but on "how can we strengthen the system". The Master's honesty after an incident is the basis for preventing future accidents.
Acil durum komutası, kaptanlığın en saf: Emergency command is the purest test of command at sea: being able to take the right decision at the moment of uncertainty and time pressure, with human lives in the balance. This ability is not innate; it comes from well-practised drills, procedures learned by heart, a sound command structure and a bridge culture open to "challenge". In a crisis the Master has to be the calmest, best prepared and clearest-thinking person on board, because at that moment everyone looks to the Master. And the best crisis management is often the preparation that prevents the crisis before it begins.
Yük operasyonunun sahada yürütülmesi Bir: Carrying out the cargo operation on site is the duty of the Chief Officer; but under ISM Code section 5 and SOLAS Chapter VI it is the Master's responsibility to verify that the operation is planned safely and carried out within the strength and stability limits. The Master can delegate the task but cannot delegate accountability. In a loading accident, PSC, class and the P&I club always ask the Master first.
The Master approves the cargo plan with his or her signature. This signature is not a formality; it is written evidence that the Master has actually reviewed the plan for consistency with the ship type, the charter party terms and the strength curves. In a dispute, the record that "the Master saw and approved the plan" is evidence that both protects and binds.
Bulk carrier'larda ana risk liquefaction: On bulk carriers the main risks are liquefaction, structural overstress and hold flooding. On tankers, fire and explosion, static electricity, inadequate inert gas and pollution stand out. On container ships the basic hazards are lashing failure, mis-declared DG and parametric rolling. The Master knows the risk profile of the ship type and concentrates supervision accordingly.
Ro-Ro ve PCC (Pure Car Carrier) gemileri: On Ro-Ro ships and PCCs (Pure Car Carriers), the openings where water can enter (bow/stern doors), low GM and the lashing of vehicles are critical. The Estonia (1994) and Golden Ray (2019) cases show the importance of stability and door safety on this type of ship.
Pre-stowage plan, stabilite/mukavemet ya: The pre-stowage plan is entered into the stability and strength software (e.g. LoadMaster, CargoMax). The Master reviews that at every stage of loading the GM, the forward, aft and midship draughts, the list, the bending moment, the shear force and, on container ships, the torsion values are within limits. Stages exceeding 85% of a limit are revised.
Bulk gemilerinde \"alternate hold loadin: If "alternate hold loading" is to be used on a bulk carrier, the combinations approved in the class-approved Loading Manual are followed strictly. The loss of the container ship MOL Comfort (2013), which broke in two, is a well-known example of how a hull girder loaded beyond its real capacity can lead to the loss of a ship.
Final cargo plan Birinci Zabit tarafında: The final cargo plan is signed by the Chief Officer, approved by the Master and handed to the chief stevedore, the terminal and the duty officer. For last-minute changes (contaminated cargo, a damaged trailer, a reefer failure), the software is run again and the plan updated. Approved printouts are kept; PSC and vetting inspections may ask for them.
2008 IS Code minimum intact stability kr: The 2008 IS Code sets the minimum intact stability criteria: the area under the GZ curve, the angle of maximum GZ, the initial GM (≥0.15 m) and the weather criterion specific to the ship type. The Master verifies that these criteria are maintained throughout loading. Too small a GM makes the ship "tender" (risk of listing); too large a GM makes her "stiff" (violent rolling, overloading of the lashings).
Free surface effect (FSC), kısmen dolu t: The free surface effect (corrected by the free surface correction, FSC) reduces the effective GM in partly filled tanks and holds. On tankers and in ballast operations the number of slack tanks is kept to a minimum. The Master checks that the FSC is entered correctly into the software.
Bending moment ve shear force, hold'lar: Bending moment and shear force depend on the distribution of cargo between the holds. Heavy cargo at the ends and light cargo in the middle causes "hogging"; the reverse causes "sagging"; both lead to hull fatigue and cracks. On bulk carriers, discharging by grab in stages carries a risk of overstress; the Master also checks the discharge sequence.
Her gemi klas onaylı bir Cargo Securing: Every ship carries an approved Cargo Securing Manual; this manual contains the MSL (Maximum Securing Load) values of the lashing equipment and the approved lashing patterns. Annex 13 of the CSS Code provides a method of calculating forces for non-standardised cargo. The Master checks that the lashing plan is consistent with the manual and adequate for the expected weather.
Container gemilerinde twist lock + lashi: On container ships the combination of twistlocks, lashing rods and turnbuckles, the tier limits and the rules for stowage on hatch covers are observed. Lashing failure is a leading cause of container losses (ONE Apus 2020, Maersk Essen 2021).
Kaptan, sefer çıkışından önce lashing ti: Before departure the Master confirms that the tightening of the lashings has been completed and that the "lashing certificate" (where applicable) is ready. On voyages where bad weather is expected, he or she gives instructions for additional lashing. For heavy lift and project cargo, an engineering calculation and class approval are required.
IMDG Code 9 ana sınıf kullanır (1 patlay: The IMDG Code uses 9 main classes (1 explosives … 9 miscellaneous). The segregation table regulates which classes may be next to each other, above each other or in adjacent holds. The Master checks the DG manifest, the packing certificate, the EmS (Emergency Schedules) and that the stowage positions comply with the segregation rules. Mis-declared DG is a hazard across the industry; the CINS circulars are followed.
Group A yükler (nickel ore, iron ore fin: Group A cargoes (nickel ore, iron ore fines, bauxite fines) can liquefy; the TML (Transportable Moisture Limit) and the cargo declaration are critical. If the TML is exceeded the Master refuses to load; otherwise the ship can capsize because of liquefaction. Group B cargoes (DRI, sulphur, coal) carry the risks of self-heating, off-gassing and CO; hold ventilation and gas measurements are needed. Group C is low risk.
Kaptan, gerektiğinde \"can test\" (IMSBC: When necessary, the Master has the "can test" (the IMSBC complementary test) carried out and does not rely blindly on the shipper's TML declaration. In the Bulk Jupiter case (2015) a bauxite cargo with too high a moisture content lost its stability (the phenomenon later described as dynamic separation); the ship capsized and 18 people died.
SOLAS VI/2 ve MSC.1/Circ.1475, her dolu: SOLAS VI/2 and MSC.1/Circ.1475 make a VGM declaration mandatory for every packed container. A container without a VGM cannot be loaded on the ship. The VGM is obtained either by weighing (Method 1) or by an approved calculation (Method 2). The Master knows that a missing VGM or implausible values are a reason to stop loading; a mis-declared weight corrupts the lashing and stability calculations (MSC Napoli, 2007, is the case usually cited).
SOLAS VI/2 uyarınca shipper, yüklemeden: Under SOLAS VI/2 the shipper must provide accurate and sufficient cargo information before loading (IMSBC group, TML, MSDS, density / stowage factor, DG class). The Master does not accept this information passively; in case of inconsistency, missing documents or a suspicious declaration, he or she asks for additional verification, has a Letter of Protest issued and, if necessary, stops loading.
Kaptan; TML aşımı şüphesi, mis-declared: The Master can stop the cargo operation because of a suspected TML exceedance, mis-declared DG, a missing VGM, exceeded stability or strength limits, unsafe practices by the terminal, a risk of pollution or the weather. This authority is the expression, in cargo operations, of the "overriding authority" in SOLAS V/34-1 and ISM 5.2.
Durdurma kararı her zaman gerekçeli ve y: A decision to stop is always made with reasons and in writing: the log book, a Letter of Protest, an e-mail to the company (DPA) and notification to the charterer through the SOF/NOR. This threefold record protects both the ship and the company in demurrage disputes and legal proceedings.
Bulk gemilerinde BLU Code, ship-shore ch: On bulk carriers the BLU Code requires the ship-shore checklist and the loading/unloading plan to be agreed and signed with the terminal. High loading rates can create overstress in a short time; if the terminal speeds up outside the plan, the Master uses the authority to slow down or stop the operation.
Yükleme/boşaltmada hose/manifold kaçakla: During loading and discharging, the risk of hose or manifold leaks, overflow and drips is monitored continuously. Even a single drop of oil spilled activates the SOPEP; the terminal and the port authority are informed at once. On tankers, ISGOTT requires the Ship-Shore Safety Checklist to be re-confirmed every watch.
Hold, tank ve kofferdam gibi kapalı alan: Entry into enclosed spaces such as holds, tanks and cofferdams is made with an enclosed space entry permit. O2, LEL, H2S and CO are measured continuously; standby personnel and a rescue plan are mandatory. Under SOLAS III/19.3.3, enclosed space entry and rescue drills are held at least every two months. The Master checks that the permit system works.
Bulk Jupiter, nem içeriği fazla olan bau: The Bulk Jupiter capsized after its bauxite cargo, which had too high a moisture content, lost its stability (18 dead). The container ship MOL Comfort broke in two because of hull strength problems. Two lessons: the shipper's declaration is questioned; strength limits are a line that is never compromised.
PCC gemisi, ballast/yük dağılımı kaynakl: A PCC capsized during a turning manoeuvre because of insufficient stability caused by the ballast and cargo distribution. Lesson: on vehicle carriers the GM margin and the ballast calculation are under the Master's direct supervision; the software printout is signed and kept before the voyage.
Yük operasyonunda kaptanın başarısı, \"h: The Master's success in cargo operations comes from disciplined approvals, cross-checks and decisions to stop, which are invisible "when everything goes well" but are the only line of defence "when something goes wrong". The Master does not stow the cargo; but the Master guarantees that the cargo does not endanger the ship and the crew.
MARPOL Annex I yağı, Annex II zararlı sı: MARPOL Annex I regulates oil, Annex II noxious liquid substances, Annex III harmful substances in packaged form, Annex IV sewage, Annex V garbage and Annex VI air emissions. For each annex the ship carries the relevant record book, certificate and management plan (IOPP, ORB, GMP, SEEMP, etc.). The Master knows which annexes apply to the ship and whether the current certificates are valid.
Kayıt defterlerindeki kayıtların doğrulu: The accuracy of the entries in the record books is the Master's personal responsibility. In the USA, magic pipe cases are generally brought on the basis of false ORB entries (false statements), resulting in prison sentences for the Master and the chief engineer and fines of millions of dollars for the company.
IOPP (Annex I), ISPP (Annex IV), IAPP ve: The IOPP (Annex I), ISPP (Annex IV), IAPP and IEEC (Annex VI) and EIAPP (for engines) certificates are subject to the cycle of initial, annual, intermediate and renewal surveys. The Master makes sure that the certificates are valid at a PSC inspection and that the supplements (equipment lists) match the equipment on board.
Makine dairesi bilge suyu, ancak 15 ppm: Engine room bilge water may be discharged only through a 15 ppm Oily Water Separator (OWS), monitored by the oil content meter, with the ship en route (in special areas the equipment must also stop the discharge automatically; in the Antarctic area no discharge is allowed). All transfers, discharges and sludge operations are entered in ORB Part I with time, position and quantity. On tankers, cargo and ballast operations are entered in ORB Part II.
Kaptan, ORB kayıtlarını periyodik olarak: The Master signs the ORB entries periodically and checks the accuracy of every page. A "magic pipe" (an OWS bypass) is the gravest environmental crime; the Master's duty is to guarantee that no such system exists on board and that the records match the actual operations exactly.
Her gemi onaylı bir SOPEP (Shipboard Oil: Every ship carries an approved SOPEP (Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergency Plan); ships carrying noxious liquid substances have an SMPEP (which also covers them). The plan contains the reporting flow (coastal state, P&I, company), the response equipment and the allocation of duties. The Master is the person who makes the first report and coordinates the response when a spill occurs. SOPEP drills are held periodically (at least once a year).
Annex V (uygulama rehberi: MEPC.295(71)): Annex V (implementation guidelines: MEPC.295(71)) divides garbage into categories (plastics, food waste, incinerator ash, operational waste, animal carcasses, fishing gear, e-waste, cargo residues). Discharging plastics into the sea is prohibited in all circumstances. Outside special areas, food waste may be discharged more than 3 NM from the nearest land if comminuted, and more than 12 NM if not comminuted.
Garbage Management Plan 100 GT ve üzeri: A Garbage Management Plan is required on ships of 100 GT and above and on ships certified to carry 15 or more persons; a Garbage Record Book on ships of 400 GT and above and on ships certified to carry 15 or more persons. The Master checks that the GRB entries reflect every discharge, incineration and delivery ashore (with the reception facility receipt) completely.
Akdeniz, Baltık, Karadeniz, Kızıldeniz v: In special areas such as the Mediterranean, the Baltic, the Black Sea, the Red Sea and the Antarctic, the discharge rules are much stricter. The Antarctic area has the strictest rules of all; for example, no oil or oily mixture may be discharged there at all. The Master knows the status of the sea area the ship is in (special area, ECA, PSSA) and passes this on to the crew in a briefing.
MARPOL VI Reg. 14, küresel yakıt sülfür: MARPOL Annex VI Reg. 14 reduced the global fuel sulphur limit to 0.50% from 1 January 2020 and to 0.10% in the ECAs (the Baltic, the North Sea, North America, the US Caribbean and, since 1 May 2025, the Mediterranean). The ship either uses compliant low-sulphur fuel (VLSFO/MGO) or achieves equivalent compliance with a scrubber (EGCS). The Master checks the Bunker Delivery Note (BDN) and the retention of the samples (12 months).
2020 Carriage Ban uyarınca, scrubber'sız: Under the 2020 carriage ban, a ship without a scrubber may not have on board (not even merely carry) fuel with a sulphur content above 0.50%. The Master guarantees that the fuel changeover on entering and leaving an ECA is made on time and that the changeover is recorded in the log book prescribed by the flag state.
2023'ten itibaren yürürlükteki EEXI (Ene: EEXI (Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index), in force since 2023, sets a one-off efficiency threshold for ships; CII (Carbon Intensity Indicator) measures the annual operational carbon intensity with an A–E rating. A ship rated D for three consecutive years or E once prepares a corrective action plan (SEEMP Part III). The Master directly affects the CII rating through slow steaming, trim optimisation and hull and propeller performance.
Kimyasal tankerlerde NLS, X/Y/Z/OS kateg: On chemical tankers, NLS are divided into categories X, Y, Z and OS. The discharge of tank washing residues is managed with the P&A (Procedures and Arrangements) Manual and the Cargo Record Book. For cargoes requiring a prewash, the operation is carried out in the presence of a surveyor. The Master checks the accuracy of the Cargo Record Book entries.
Lağım suyu şu koşullarla deşarj edilebil: Sewage may be discharged as follows: comminuted and disinfected by an approved system, more than 3 NM from the nearest land; untreated sewage (from a holding tank) more than 12 NM from the nearest land, with the ship en route at not less than 4 knots and at a moderate rate; effluent from an approved sewage treatment plant without a distance limit, provided it leaves no visible floating solids or discoloration. Stricter rules apply to passenger ships in special areas such as the Baltic. The Master checks that the STP is in working order and that the discharge records are kept properly.
BWM Convention, istilacı türlerin taşınm: To prevent the transfer of invasive species, the BWM Convention introduces the D-1 standard (ballast water exchange) and the final D-2 standard (the ballast water performance standard, met by treatment). Ships are fitted with IMO type-approved BWMS (UV, electrochlorination, ozone). The Ballast Water Record Book records every ballast uptake, discharge and exchange; the Ballast Water Management Plan is specific to the ship.
Kaptan, BWMS'in çalışır durumda olduğunu: The Master checks that the BWMS is in working order, that D-2 compliance is achieved and that the BWRB is kept correctly. The USA (USCG) has its own approval regime; ships entering US waters need additional compliance.
AFS Convention, TBT içeren zararlı anti-: The AFS Convention prohibits harmful anti-fouling systems containing TBT; under recent amendments cybutryne has also been prohibited. The ship carries an AFS certificate or declaration. After dry-docking the Master verifies that the paints are compliant and that the certificate is up to date.
Hull biofouling, hem CII performansını h: Hull biofouling affects both CII performance and the risk of invasive species; some jurisdictions (New Zealand, California) require a biofouling management record. The Master finds out in advance the regional environmental rules of the area the ship is going to (ECA, the EU Emissions Trading System, regional speed limits) and plans compliance.
ORB, GRB ve BWRB kayıtları PSC, klas ve: The ORB, GRB and BWRB entries are the first documents looked at in PSC, class and vetting (SIRE, CDI) inspections. An inconsistency between the records and the actual operations (e.g. a mismatch between the sludge quantity and the tank level) is a reason for a "deficiency" or detention. The Master guarantees that the records reflect the truth and that no retrospective "corrections" are made.
ABD APPS rejimi, kirliliği ihbar eden mü: The US APPS regime gives a reward (part of the fine) to crew members who report pollution. This means that it is impossible to hide falsified records. By building an open and honest environmental culture on board, the Master stays on the safe side both legally and ethically.
Bir döküntü veya ihlalde kaptan; SOPEP r: In the event of a spill or a violation, the Master informs the nearest coastal state, the port authority, the company (DPA) and the P&I Club using the SOPEP reporting format. The response is documented with the log book and photographs and video. Early, honest and complete reporting is the most effective attitude for limiting penalties and liability.
Çevresel uyumlulukta kaptanın gücü tekno: In environmental compliance the Master's strength lies not in technology but in honest records and the culture on board. A correctly kept ORB is the difference between a fine of millions of dollars and a PSC inspection of a few hours. The Master treats protecting the marine environment not only as a legal obligation but as part of professional honour.
Bayrak devleti, SOLAS Chapter I gereğinc: Under SOLAS Chapter I, the flag state confirms with certificates that the ship complies with the international conventions; it often delegates this authority to a Recognized Organization (RO — e.g. a class society). Statutory surveys produce convention certificates such as the IOPP, SafCon, SafEquip, ISSC and SMC. Class surveys, on the other hand, check the structural integrity of the ship and the compliance of the machinery and equipment with the class rules, and maintain the Class Certificate.
İki katman pratikte iç içe geçer: bir kl: In practice the two layers are intertwined: a class surveyor can close both statutory and class items in the same visit. The Master must know which item belongs to which regime, because a condition of class (CoC) or a memorandum has a different timetable and consequence from a statutory deficiency. If a CoC is not closed in time, class is suspended, which automatically takes the ship out of service and out of insurance cover.
PSC, bir liman devletinin (Paris/Tokyo M: PSC is a legal enforcement mechanism through which a port state (Paris/Tokyo MOU, USCG, AMSA, Black Sea MOU, etc.) inspects foreign-flagged ships in its waters for compliance with international standards. PSC has sanctions: deficiency, detention, banning. The aim is safety and the environment; the outcome is public and visible on platforms such as Equasis.
Vetting ise ticari bir kabul sürecidir;: Vetting, by contrast, is a commercial acceptance process: a charterer or cargo owner (e.g. the major oil companies that are OCIMF members, or RightShip in dry bulk) carries out a risk assessment before chartering the ship. Vetting has no legal enforcement power, but its commercial sanction is very harsh: a negative SIRE report or a low RightShip score can exclude the ship from a whole commercial segment. The practical consequence for the Master: in PSC the aim is "to avoid detention"; in vetting the aim is "to keep the ship charterable at all times".
Tipik bir kuru yük gemisinde taşınması g: The main certificates to be carried on a typical dry cargo ship are: Cargo Ship Safety Construction (SafCon), Cargo Ship Safety Equipment (SafEquip), Cargo Ship Safety Radio (SafRadio), IOPP (MARPOL Annex I), IAPP (Annex VI), ISPP (Annex IV — sewage), IEEC (Energy Efficiency), ISSC (ISPS), SMC (ISM), the MLC certificate, IBWMC (Ballast Water), Tonnage, Load Line, the Minimum Safe Manning Document and the Bunker Convention insurance certificate (and, for oil tankers, the CLC certificate). Most are valid for 5 years but are subject to annual, intermediate and renewal surveys and their windows.
Kaptanın kritik kavramı \"survey window\: A critical concept for the Master is the "survey window": it forms a window from 3 months before to 3 months after the anniversary date (±3 months for the annual survey). The renewal survey must be completed within the 3 months before the expiry date. Going outside the window breaks the harmonised survey regime, and a certificate falling "out of window" directly produces a deficiency at PSC. The Master must plan the port rotation with the company so as to catch the survey windows.
ISM rejiminde iki belge vardır: şirkete: The ISM regime has two documents: the company's Document of Compliance (DOC) and the ship's Safety Management Certificate (SMC). The SMC on board is valid only as long as the company holds a valid DOC; the Master must verify that a certified copy of the DOC is on board and that the ship type is listed in the scope of the DOC (e.g. if it says "bulk carrier", the ship cannot trade as a tanker).
ISSC için de benzer mantık geçerlidir: g: A similar logic applies to the ISSC: an approved ship security plan (SSP) and working CSO/PFSO coordination are the foundation of the ISSC. When an inspector at PSC sees the SMC, he or she tests the question "is the SMS really working on board?" with the near-miss records, the drill records and the closure rates of corrective actions. What is inspected is not the certificate hanging on the wall but whether the system behind it is alive.
Paris MOU New Inspection Regime, her gem: The Paris MOU New Inspection Regime assigns every ship a Ship Risk Profile (SRP): Low Risk Ship (LRS), Standard Risk Ship (SRS) or High Risk Ship (HRS). The profile is calculated from the ship type and age, flag performance (black/grey/white list), class/RO performance, the company's previous record of deficiencies and detentions, and the findings of recent inspections. LRS ships are inspected every 24–36 months, HRS ships every 5–6 months.
Kaptanın pratik çıkarımı şudur: geminin: The practical conclusion for the Master is this: the ship's past deficiencies and the company's record directly determine how often she is inspected today. A single detention can lower the company's performance rating (e.g. from high or medium to low or very low) and increase the likelihood of every ship in the fleet being targeted. This is why the Master is not content with saying "I passed my own inspection"; he or she knows that every finding affects the company's record and the risk of the fleet.
Bir PSC denetimi tipik olarak initial in: A PSC inspection typically begins with an initial inspection: a check of the certificates, the general condition of the ship (general impression) and first contact with the crew. If "clear grounds" arise — for example a missing certificate, visibly defective equipment, crew who do not know their basic duties — the inspection is escalated to a more detailed inspection. For certain ship types and ages an expanded inspection is mandatory anyway.
Kaptan, \"general impression\" faktörünü: The Master must not underestimate the "general impression" factor: a rusty deck, lighting that does not work, an untidy lifeboat station, watertight doors left open, a dirty engine room — all of these give the inspector the impression that "the system on this ship is weak" and deepen the inspection. The impression made in the first 15 minutes sets the tone and the length of the inspection.
Her yıl Paris ve Tokyo MOU, belirli bir: Every year the Paris and Tokyo MOUs run a Concentrated Inspection Campaign (CIC) focusing on a particular theme: in the past, themes such as STCW rest hours, MARPOL Annex VI, fire safety, ISM, crew familiarisation and ballast water management have been chosen. During the CIC period a CIC questionnaire is applied to every ship in addition to the standard inspection. The Master must find out that year's CIC theme in advance and prepare the related files, records and equipment tests specifically.
CIC'in incelikli yanı, normalde detentio: The subtle side of a CIC is that a finding that would not normally be a reason for detention can turn into a deficiency when an item in the CIC questionnaire is answered "No". For example, in a ballast water CIC the failure to keep the approved operating record of the BWMS, or in a fire safety CIC missing maintenance records of the fixed CO2 system, are examined throughout the campaign far more closely than usual.
Her deficiency, bir konu koduna (örn. 01: Each deficiency is linked to an area code (e.g. 01 certificates, 04 emergency systems, 07 fire safety, 10 safety of navigation, 15 ISM) and to one or more action codes. The action code says what the inspector requires of the ship: 17 = "rectify before departure", 15 = "rectify at next port", 16 = "rectify within 14 days", 18 = "rectify within 3 months" and, the gravest, 30 = "grounds for detention / ship detained".
Kaptan, bir bulgunun action kodunu rapor: The Master must always read the action code of a finding before signing the report, because the difference between "rectify before departure" (17) and "detained" (30) is an operational and commercial chasm that keeps the ship from sailing. A code 30 is a sign not only of that finding but of a systemic doubt about the safe operation of the ship.
Detention'lar genellikle \"emniyeti, çev: Detentions usually arise from findings that "directly threaten safety, the environment or life": lifeboat launching appliances or davits that do not work, a defective emergency fire pump, an oily water separator discharging overboard with the 15 ppm control bypassed, an invalid or missing main certificate, a back-up steering gear system that does not work, open or obstructed watertight integrity, a serious breach of rest hours and a crew unable to demonstrate their basic emergency duties.
Kaptanın hafife almaması gereken nokta,: A point the Master must not underestimate is that "the sum of several small findings" can lead to detention just as much as "one big failure". If the inspector sees a picture of findings that are each small but together prove that the SMS has collapsed, he or she can detain the ship under the ISM (code 15). In other words, the ship can be detained on the grounds that "none of them is fatal on its own, but together they show that there is no system".
SIRE 2.0, OCIMF'in 2024'te tam yürürlüğe: SIRE 2.0 is OCIMF's new tanker vetting regime, fully introduced in 2024. Instead of the old static VIQ, it works with tablets, a question bank and a vessel-specific risk profile. When the inspector arrives on board, he or she sees the set of questions the system has selected for that ship; the questions are divided into the Hardware (equipment), Process (procedures and records) and Human (crew competence) dimensions. The weight given to the human factor has greatly increased the importance of the interviews with the Master and the officers.
Kaptanın SIRE 2.0 hazırlığı, dosya düzel: The Master's preparation for SIRE 2.0 goes beyond tidying files: an officer must be able to answer the question "how do you apply this procedure?" by describing the real practice on his or her own ship. Because of photographic evidence and the real-time recording system, "show it and put it away" is not possible. In SIRE 2.0 negative findings are reported as "observations"; each observation must be closed by the company with a root cause and corrective action, otherwise the way to the next charter is not open.
RightShip, ağırlıklı olarak dökme yük (b: RightShip is the platform through which charterers in the dry bulk segment mainly (traditionally iron ore, coal, grain) make their ship acceptance decisions. It assigns a ship a Safety Score (1 to 5, similar to stars) and also a GHG Rating (A–G, rating the ship's carbon efficiency relative to comparable ships). A low safety score or a poor GHG rating leads to the ship dropping off the nomination lists of the big mining and energy companies.
RightShip kabulü için RISQ (RightShip'in: For RightShip acceptance a physical inspection based on RISQ (RightShip's inspection questionnaire) may also be carried out. The Master's practical task is to ensure, together with the company, that the ship's data on the RightShip platform (survey dates, PSC history, accident and incident records) is up to date and correct, and to take every finding seriously, knowing in particular that PSC detentions pull the score down for months.
CDI (Chemical Distribution Institute), k: CDI (Chemical Distribution Institute) is a vetting and inspection regime for chemical and gas tankers similar to that of OCIMF; the CDI-Marine report is decisive in chemical cargo owners' ship acceptance decisions. SIRE for oil tankers, CDI for chemicals and gas, RightShip for dry bulk — the Master must master the inspection logic and reporting cycle of the programme of the segment in which the ship trades.
Tüm bu programların ortak paydası şudur:: The common denominator of all these programmes is this: vetting is not a snapshot of a "moment" but a continuous record and performance history. A ship may be rejected because of unclosed observations in her past reports even if she passes an inspection brilliantly. The Master must therefore manage vetting not as an "event" but as a "state" maintained every day.
Kaptan, beklenen PSC veya vetting öncesi: Before an expected PSC inspection or vetting, the Master carries out a systematic internal audit using the ship's own VIQ/RISQ/PSC checklist. This audit covers the deck, the engine room, the life-saving appliances (LSA), the fire-fighting appliances (FFA), the bridge, the paper and electronic records and the competence of the crew. The findings are entered in a "snag list"; each item is assigned to a responsible person and a deadline.
İyi bir self-audit, \"denetçi gözüyle\": A good self-audit is done "through the inspector's eyes"; that is, the Master must learn to look at his or her own ship as an outside inspector. Familiarity with the team (familiarity bias) makes real findings invisible; therefore having the self-audit done by a different officer, or a cross-audit (the chief officer audits the engine room, the 2nd engineer the deck), reduces blind spots.
Hazırlığın en kritik ve en çok ihmal edi: The most critical and most neglected part of the preparation is preparing the crew for the inspection. Every crew member must be able to show his or her muster station, fire and abandon ship duties, and the use of the EEBD and immersion suit. When the inspector stops a randomly chosen rating (an oiler, an AB) and asks "what do you do when the fire alarm sounds?", an unhesitating and correct answer is the strongest proof that the system works.
Kaptan, denetim öncesi bir \"tatbikat br: Before the inspection the Master holds a preparation briefing: with crew members who face a language barrier, the English wording of the key answers is refreshed, and the location and testing of critical equipment are repeated. But this is not imposing rote learning; it is reminding people of what they really know, because an answer learned by heart but not understood falls apart at the first follow-up question and creates distrust in the inspector.
Denetçi gemiye geldiğinde kaptan veya gö: When the inspector arrives on board, the Master or a senior officer designated by the Master meets him or her, gives a safety briefing (PPE, restricted areas, emergencies) and provides a suitable escort throughout the inspection. The inspector is never left alone; in each area the person in charge of that department (the chief officer on deck, the chief engineer in the engine room) is present. The escort is not there to "watch" the inspector but to direct questions to the right person and put a finding in context at once.
İletişimde altın kural: sorulmayanı söyl: The golden rule of communication: do not volunteer what is not asked; answer what is asked honestly and clearly. Crew members should not guess on a subject they do not know but should say "let me check and give you the exact information". A lie or a contradictory statement is far more dangerous than a single finding, because it fundamentally shakes the inspector's trust in the ship and pulls the inspection into a defensive depth.
Bir bulgu yanlış veya haksız görünüyorsa: If a finding seems wrong or unfair, the Master can discuss it during the closing meeting respectfully, with reasons and on the basis of documents; the discussion must not become personal but must proceed on the basis of the regulations and the evidence. If the inspector is convinced, the finding may be dropped before it enters the report; if not, the Master must sign the report, but the signature means "receipt of the report", not "acceptance of the finding".
PSC raporunda kaptan, deficiency'lerin a: In the PSC report the Master must read carefully the action codes of the deficiencies, the rectification periods and the notes on the ship. In the case of a code 30 (detention), the Master at once informs the company, the DPA, the flag state, class and the P&I/H&M side, and coordinates the survey and re-inspection process needed to lift the detention. Where justified, a formal appeal or review of the detention can be requested within the time limits set by national law and the MOU.
