Her deficiency veya observation için ISM: For every deficiency or observation a root cause analysis is carried out under the ISM. Using "5 Whys" or similar methods, the managerial or systemic cause beneath the surface technical failure is found. For example, the root cause of the finding "the emergency fire pump did not work" is often not the pump itself but a maintenance item missing from the PMS, untrained personnel or an insufficient stock of spare parts.
Kaptanın burada hassas olması gereken no: The point on which the Master must be careful here is the difference between "blame" and "root cause". "The AB was negligent" is not a root cause but an accusation; the real root cause may be "this item was not in the AB's job description" or "familiarisation was inadequate". RCA based on a just culture is a precondition of an honest reporting culture that does not hide the real cause.
RCA'nın çıktısı, bir düzeltici aksiyon (: The output of the RCA is a plan of corrective action (removing the present problem) and preventive action (preventing recurrence). While the corrective action is "repair the pump", the preventive action may be "add this test to the PMS every 3 months, train the personnel concerned, tie the spare part to a minimum stock level". Each action is assigned to a responsible person, a deadline and evidence of closure (photo, test report, training record).
Kaptan, tüm bulgu-RCA-CA/PA döngüsünü şi: The Master enters the whole finding–RCA–CA/PA cycle into the company's SMS reporting system (usually a non-conformity / CAR form) and passes it to the DPA. This record is not just a bureaucratic requirement; it is the concrete answer to the question "how did you close your last finding?" at the next inspection, and an input to the company's management review. Unclosed actions come up again and again at vetting and PSC.
Denetçinin en sevdiği teknik, farklı kay: The inspector's favourite technique is cross-checking different records. A transfer in the Oil Record Book must be consistent with the engine room logs, the sounding records and the bunker delivery notes (BDN). The deck log, the GMDSS log, the ECDIS route history and the passage plan must not contradict each other. One record contradicting another raises the inspector's suspicion that "something is being hidden here" and pulls the inspection into a forensic depth.
Rest hours kayıtları özellikle hassastır: Rest hour records are particularly sensitive: meeting the STCW A-VIII/1 and MLC limits (≥10 hours in 24 hours, ≥77 hours in 7 days) "on paper" while breaching them in reality comes to light when the inspector cross-checks them against the port log, the gangway watch and the cargo operation records. Rest hour sheets that "look perfect but are unrealistic" are a red flag for the inspector.
Kayıt sahteciliği — özellikle ORB'de \"m: Falsification of records — especially concealing a "magic pipe" in the ORB (oily water discharged overboard bypassing the OWS) — is among the crimes punished most severely in maritime law. In the USA, under APPS (Act to Prevent Pollution from Ships), entering a US port with a false ORB is a crime in itself even if the pollution did not actually occur in US waters; fines of millions of dollars, imprisonment of the Master and denial of departure clearance for the ship can follow.
Kaptan için temel ilke şudur: bir bulgu,: The basic principle for the Master is this: a finding recorded honestly is a manageable problem; concealed, it turns into a crime that ends careers and freedom. Preparing for an inspection does not mean "making an ugly truth look good" but "correcting the truth before the inspection and documenting it honestly". Falsification is a risk greater than any deficiency could ever create.
Kaptan için \"denetime hazır gemi\", den: For the Master, an "inspection-ready ship" is not a ship hastily tidied up on the morning of the inspection but a ship kept in an inspectable condition every day. When the discipline of the certificate matrix, the honesty of the self-audit, the depth of the root cause analysis and the genuine competence of the crew all come together, PSC and vetting are merely outside confirmation of this continuous preparation. The best Master is the one who saw and corrected what the inspector sees long before; for him or her the inspection is not an examination but the confirmation of a result already known.
ISM Code madde 6, şirketin geminin \"uyg: ISM Code section 6 requires the company to ensure that the ship is manned with "qualified, certificated and medically fit" seafarers. The person who applies this section on board is the Master: it is the Master's responsibility to verify that every crew member is competent for his or her duties, holds the required certificates and has been properly familiarised before starting work.
Madde 6 ayrıca, geminin emniyeti ve çevr: Section 6 also requires ensuring that duties critical to the safety of the ship and the protection of the environment are understood by the personnel; this covers a common working language, the comprehensibility of instructions and the effectiveness of training. In a multinational crew, the adequacy of the common working language (usually English) is a subject questioned directly in ISM audits and accident analyses.
STCW Reg. I/14, şirketleri gemiye atanan: STCW Reg. I/14 holds companies responsible for ensuring that the certificates of seafarers assigned to the ship are valid and appropriate to their duties, that records complying with STCW are kept on board, and that familiarisation and emergency coordination are provided. The extension of this responsibility on board is the Master; the company sets the policy, the Master applies it on site and reports deviations.
Pratikte bu, kaptanın her join eden müre: In practice this means that the Master checks, physically or electronically, the STCW certificates of every crew member who joins (CoC — Certificate of Competency, CoP — Certificate of Proficiency, GMDSS, tanker endorsement, advanced fire fighting, medical first aid, etc.). If a missing certificate or one about to expire is found, the company is notified at once; employing a person without a certificate in a duty that requires one is both a breach of STCW and a serious insurance risk.
SOLAS V/14 ve IMO Res. A.1047(27) uyarın: Under SOLAS V/14 and IMO Res. A.1047(27), every ship carries a Minimum Safe Manning Document issued by the flag state. This document defines the minimum manning — by position and certificate level — needed for the safe navigation of the ship, the safety of life, the protection of the marine environment and safe operation. The Master must ensure that the actual manning on board never falls below this document.
MSMD bir \"yeterlilik\" değil \"asgari\": The MSMD is a document of the "minimum", not of "adequacy"; on routes with heavy cargo operations, frequent port calls, canal transits or tiring passages, the minimum manning may in practice be insufficient. If the Master finds that the actual workload is forcing the minimum crew into breaches of rest hours, he or she must report this to the company with reasons and request additional personnel or rotation. A crew at minimum manning that is "compliant on paper" but "tired in reality" is the classic beginning of an accident chain.
Kaptan, kadronun yorgunluk seviyesini sü: The Master continuously monitors the fatigue level of the crew; the STCW A-VIII/1 and MLC limits (at least 10 hours of rest in 24 hours, at least 77 hours in 7 days) are only a floor, not a target. Intensive port rotations, frequently broken watches and critical operations (cargo, anchoring, canal) increase fatigue cumulatively. Before critical operations the Master actually verifies that the key personnel are rested.
Manning planlaması ile rest hours yöneti: Manning planning and rest hour management are two sides of the same coin: an insufficient crew makes breaches of rest hours mathematically inevitable. If the Master has to choose between "making the records look clean" and "really letting the crew rest", he or she must choose the latter and send the company a written request for the manning or rotation that would make the former possible.
STCW ve ISM gereği, gemiye yeni katılan: Under STCW and the ISM, everyone newly joining the ship — whether a seafarer, a riding crew member or a contractor — goes through a basic safety familiarisation before starting work: he or she learns the muster station, the alarm signals, where the lifejacket and immersion suit are and how to put them on, the escape routes, the watertight doors and the basic "dos and don'ts". This familiarisation must be completed before the ship berths or before the first critical moments of the voyage.
Kaptanın sorumluluğu, bu tanıtımın \"for: The Master's responsibility is to ensure that this familiarisation is not just "getting a form signed". The newcomer must really know where to go when the alarm sounds; this is why good familiarisation includes a physical walk-through on board: the person actually walks to the muster station, is shown the nearest exit and puts on a lifejacket with it in hand.
Genel tanıtımın ötesinde, her mürettebat: Beyond the general familiarisation, every crew member is familiarised with the equipment specific to his or her duties: the officer of the watch with the make of ECDIS on board, the radar, the autopilot and the GMDSS console; the engineer with the ship's main engine, auxiliary systems and alarm panel. An officer keeping a watch alone without type-specific training is a recurring cause of accidents in MAIB reports.
Kaptan, göreve özgü familiarization'ı bi: The Master runs duty-specific familiarisation through a checklist and a responsible senior officer (the chief officer for the deck, the chief engineer for the engine room). The critical point is timing: a person may take on a duty alone (e.g. a solo navigational watch) only after familiarisation has been completed and his or her competence confirmed. The "he will learn on his first watch" approach is unacceptable.
Birçok şirket SMS'i, periyodik competenc: Many company SMSs provide for periodic competency assessment forms: a structured, observation-based tool that scores particular competence items and marks the areas for development. The Master or a senior officer designated by the Master carries out this assessment each period, shares the results with the person and links them to a development plan.
Değerlendirmenin değeri, dürüstlüğüyle d: The value of the assessment is in direct proportion to its honesty. A Master who gives "everyone high marks" both blocks the development of that person and misleads the company about the real risk. Conversely, an assessment that only points out weaknesses damages morale. A good assessment is a balanced tool that records strengths and links each area for development to a concrete action.
SOLAS Chapter III ve ISM madde 8, düzenl: SOLAS Chapter III and ISM section 8 make regular drills mandatory: abandon ship and fire drills every month (within 24 hours of leaving port if more than 25% of the crew did not take part in drills the previous month), enclosed space entry and rescue drills at least every two months, and also damage control, oil spill (SOPEP), man overboard, steering gear failure, security (ISPS) and other scenarios. The Master keeps the schedule of these drills and records that they have actually been carried out.
Tatbikatın amacı kayıt doldurmak değil,: The purpose of a drill is not to fill in records but to build muscle memory for a moment of crisis. Good drills are therefore realistic: the scenario is changed (the same monthly "lower the lifeboat" routine becomes rote), difficulty is added (one person counts as "injured", one exit is assumed "blocked") and an honest debrief is held afterwards. El Faro and similar accidents showed that rote and unrealistic drills are of no use in a crisis.
Her tatbikatın asıl değeri debrief'tedir: The real value of every drill lies in the debrief: what went well, where time was lost, which equipment did not work as expected, which role remained unclear. The Master runs the debrief not as an "assessment exam" but as an open, no-blame learning session; junior crew must be able to share an error rather than hide it. The lessons learned shape the scenario of the next drill.
Onboard training, drill'lerle sınırlı de: Onboard training is not limited to drills: junior personnel are developed continuously with toolbox talks, short training videos, CBT (computer-based training) modules, hands-on lessons on equipment and the "shadow watch" (a supervised watch). The Master ties training to a schedule and records it, because PSC and vetting examine training records as evidence that the system is alive.
Bridge Resource Management ve Engine-roo: Bridge Resource Management and Engine-room Resource Management became mandatory competences with the STCW Manila amendments. The basic principles are a clear division of roles (who has the con, who navigates, who keeps the lookout, who handles communications), closed-loop communication (an order given is confirmed by being repeated back), sharing situational awareness within the team, and error-trapping mechanisms (cross-checking, monitoring).
Kaptanın buradaki rolü çift yönlüdür: he: The Master's role here is twofold: to lead as the head of the team, and to create an environment in which the team can "challenge" him or her. A junior officer being able to say "the CPA looks too close to me" is a sign that the team really works. If this culture is not built, even the most competent team will miss the danger seen by a junior who stays silent.
Etkili ekip yönetimi, hatanın kaçınılmaz: Effective team management accepts that error is inevitable and concentrates on catching it early. A "just culture" separates deliberate violations from human error: human error that is reported is not punished but learned from; reckless risk-taking or deliberate breaking of rules, however, has consequences. By striking this balance, the Master ensures that near misses and errors are reported rather than hidden.
Near-miss raporlamasının canlı olması, b: Lively near-miss reporting is the most reliable indicator of a ship's safety culture. A ship from which no near miss is ever reported is not a ship where "everything is perfect" but one where "nothing is reported because of fear". The Master encourages reporting, protects the person who reports and draws a systemic lesson from every report.
Çoğu şirket, mürettebatın gemide kalış s: Most companies provide for an appraisal form filled in at the end of a crew member's time on board or periodically. This form scores dimensions such as technical competence, safety awareness, teamwork, leadership, discipline and development potential, and is the basis for decisions on promotion and re-employment. The Master or a senior officer makes an assessment based on observation, supported by concrete examples and shared with the person.
Adil appraisal, kişiye yüz yüze geri bil: A fair appraisal is given to the person with face-to-face feedback; it should not be a surprise. A Master who manages well gives feedback continuously throughout the period, so that the appraisal is only a written summary of what has been said all along. An unfair or arbitrary appraisal affects that person's career and also damages the sense of fairness on board, and therefore morale.
Appraisal yalnızca bir not değil, bir ge: An appraisal is not just a mark but the start of a development plan. For a strong junior officer, the Master can plan steps to prepare for promotion (e.g. more supervised manoeuvring, responsibility for coastal navigation, mentoring in paperwork). Conversely, for a person who is struggling, concrete improvement goals and support are defined.
Kaptanın halefiyet (succession) perspekt: The Master is expected to have a succession perspective: today's second officer is tomorrow's chief officer; today's chief officer is tomorrow's Master. A good Master sees training people who could fill his or her own place not as a threat but as a professional duty. This is the only real source of sustainable competence for the fleet.
Disiplin, ceza değil, paylaşılan standar: Discipline is not punishment but the upholding of shared standards. The company SMS and the employment agreements (SEA/CBA) provide a fair procedure for disciplinary action (warning, investigation, the right of defence, records); the Master applies this procedure consistently and without arbitrariness. Reacting differently to different people for the same breach is what destroys authority fastest.
Disiplinin amacı, bir kişiyi cezalandırm: The purpose of discipline is less to punish one person than to remind the whole team of how seriously the standard is taken. In serious cases (violence, drunkenness, desertion, a positive D&A test) the Master coordinates with the company at once; but most everyday matters are resolved with an early, private and fair conversation, without the need for a formal procedure. A good Master uses formal discipline as a last resort.
Modern bir gemi mürettebatı genellikle ç: A modern ship's crew is usually multinational and multicultural. The Master ensures respect for differences of language, culture, religion and tradition, the prohibition of discrimination (MLC) and equal treatment. In an isolated environment, morale is maintained through the quality of the food, rest, internet and communication facilities, a fair distribution of work and a respectful atmosphere. Low morale is as dangerous an accident factor as fatigue.
Kaptan, mürettebatın refahını (welfare): The Master must treat the welfare of the crew — long contracts, missing their families, isolation, mental health — as a visible priority. An open-door policy, a complaint procedure that really works and a person's ability to raise his or her voice safely when struggling are required by the MLC and are the basis of operational safety. A happy and respected crew is a safe crew.
Mürettebat rotasyonu (crew change) sürek: Crew rotation (crew change) carries a constant risk of losing information; the handover of the Master, the chief officer and the chief engineer in particular is critical. A good handover covers a realistic account of open issues, unclosed findings, ongoing maintenance items, charterer and company instructions, the particularities of critical equipment and the dynamics of the team. A written handover note is standard and, where possible, the handover is made face to face (with an overlap).
Kaptan değişiminde, gelen kaptanın gemiy: When the Master changes, the first days are vital for the incoming Master to grasp the ship, the SMS, the crew and the open risks quickly. An incomplete handover puts the new Master into a risk he or she does not know about; this is why the outgoing Master is obliged to make an honest and complete handover rather than hiding problems to "look good".
Kaptanın kadro ve eğitim yönetimi, tek b: The Master's management of manning and training goes beyond the limits of a single ship; the appraisals he or she gives, the officers he or she trains and the competence gaps he or she reports feed the company's fleet-wide human resources planning. By reporting training needs and certificate gaps to the company regularly, the Master ensures that the next rotation is better prepared.
Sonuçta gemideki insan kaynağı, en pahal: In the end, the human resource on board is a more critical resource than the most expensive equipment: even the most advanced ship is unsafe with a crew that is not competent, rested and in good spirits. The Master's skill in managing manning and training is measured by a crew that works quietly, does not fall apart in a crisis and keeps improving.
Kaptanın kadro ve eğitim yönetimindeki b: The Master's success in managing manning and training is not a shiny list but a reality that shows itself in a crisis: everyone knowing his or her place when the alarm sounds, a junior officer being able to speak up about a danger he or she sees, a tired crew having been rested beforehand, and an error being reported rather than hidden. None of these results is a coincidence; all are the product of the disciplined follow-up of competence, genuine familiarisation, realistic drills and fair leadership that the Master maintains every day. A good Master knows that even the best equipment comes down to people, and counts training those people as the most important duty.
Kaptan, geminin yasal temsilcisidir (mas: The Master is the legal representative of the ship (master as agent). A document the Master signs is not just a confirmation; it is a legal undertaking binding the ship, the shipowner and in some cases the charterer. The signature on a bill of lading (B/L) starts the contract of carriage, the signature on the NOR starts the laytime clock, and a letter of protest is a declaration reserving rights against the other party. The Master must therefore know the legal consequence of every document he or she signs.
İmza atılırken \"for and on behalf of th: When signing, qualifications such as "for and on behalf of the Master" or "as agent only" can limit the Master's personal liability; but these wordings must be used carefully. If the Master signs documents prepared by the agent without reading them, this later leads to the presumption that "the Master approved", which is hard to reverse.
Belgeler iki ana kategoriye ayrılır: (a): Documents fall into two main categories: (a) official books made mandatory by the flag state or international conventions (official log book, oil record book, garbage record book, rest hour records); (b) commercial and operational documents (NOR, SOF, mate's receipt, manifest). In official books no page number may be skipped, nothing may be erased and nothing may be filled in retrospectively; errors are struck through with a single line and initialled.
Bu ayrım önemlidir çünkü resmi defterler: This distinction matters because falsification of official books falls under criminal law and can lead to PSC detention. In the USA, companies have been fined millions of dollars for falsifying the Oil Record Book (the magic pipe cases).
STCW sertifikası asgari standardı belgel: An STCW certificate documents the minimum standard; but two officers with the same certificate can show very different competence in practice. From the first watches the Master observes each officer's real level: discipline in fixing the position, application of COLREG, command of the equipment, speed of decision-making and behaviour under pressure. This observation builds a real competence profile of each officer.
Bu değerlendirme yargılamak için değil,: This assessment is not for judging but for identifying training needs. If an officer's radar plotting is weak, the Master treats this not as a "fault" but as an opportunity for targeted onboard training. The competence profile determines who may work under supervision and who without supervision in which operation; this is the basis of the allocation of duties and of risk management.
Official Log Book (ÖLB), bayrak devletin: The Official Log Book (OLB) is an official book kept in the format of the flag state. Its contents vary with the flag but typically include: crew sign-on and sign-off records, births and deaths, disciplinary events, draught records, instructions from the maritime administration, drill records, the results of official inspections and important events. Every entry must be dated and timed and signed by the officer concerned or the Master.
Ölüm, ciddi yaralanma, doğum, kaybolma (: Events such as a death, a serious injury, a birth or a disappearance (man overboard) are entered in the OLB at once and usually require a witness signature. These entries are primary evidence in consular, insurance and judicial proceedings. A back-dated entry destroys its value as evidence in law and exposes the Master to personal liability.
Deck Log Book, vardiya zabitlerince saat: The Deck Log Book is the operational log of the voyage, kept hour by hour by the officers of the watch. Position, course, speed, weather (wind, sea state, barometer, visibility), engine telegraph changes, anchoring and weighing anchor, pilot embarkation and disembarkation, draughts, ballast operations and important communications are entered. Each watch is signed by the officer taking over.
Deck log, çatışma, karaya oturma veya ağ: After a collision, a grounding or heavy weather damage, the deck log is the basic source for the sea protest and the P&I process. For this reason, during and after an incident the log entries must be kept in as much detail as possible, and helm orders and engine orders must be recorded with time stamps. A log entry that contradicts the VDR (Voyage Data Recorder) data damages credibility in a case.
Bayrak devletleri giderek elektronik kay: Flag states increasingly allow electronic record books (e-OLB, e-ORB); the 2020 amendments to MARPOL formally recognised the use of electronic record books. In a digital system, too, an unalterable audit trail, time stamps and identification of the authorised user are essential. The Master confirms that the system is approved (type-approved) and can produce a legible printout at an inspection.
Deck log ile VDR/ECDIS kayıtları arasınd: Consistency between the deck log and the VDR/ECDIS records is critical. In a dispute, the first documents the parties ask for are the VDR download, the ECDIS playback and the deck log. After a critical event the Master must ensure that the VDR data is preserved (save/lock) without being overwritten; otherwise evidence is lost.
NOR, geminin yükleme/boşaltma için her b: The NOR is the document notifying the charterer or receiver that the ship is ready in all respects to load or discharge, and it starts the laytime clock. For the NOR to be valid, the ship must be physically and legally ready (free pratique granted, customs formalities completed, access to the cargo open). An NOR tendered too early or invalidly upsets the laytime calculation and leads to demurrage/despatch disputes.
Charter party'de \"WIPON, WIBON, WIFPON,: The "WIPON, WIBON, WIFPON, WCCON" (whether in port / in berth / in free pratique / customs cleared or not) clauses in the charter party determine when the NOR may be tendered. The Master must know these clauses and tender the NOR in writing at the right time and to the right party (usually the charterer and the agent). The time of tender (date and time) is very important.
SOF, limandaki tüm olayların (varış, dem: The SOF is the time-stamped chronological record of all events in port (arrival, anchoring, berthing, NOR tendered, start and completion of cargo, waiting times, weather stoppages, breakdowns). The agent prepares it; the Master checks and signs it. The SOF is the basis of the demurrage/despatch calculation through the time sheet; for this reason the cause of every delay (rain, no cargo, awaiting documents) must be written clearly.
Kaptan, SOF'taki çelişkili veya gemi ale: Before signing, the Master corrects any contradictory entry or entry against the ship in the SOF; if it is not corrected, he or she signs with the remark "signed under protest, time as per ship's log". This remark ensures that the ship's records are taken as the basis in any later arbitration.
Mate's Receipt, yükün gemiye alındığını: The Mate's Receipt is the preliminary document showing that the cargo has been received on board, and it forms the basis of the B/L. Reservations about the cargo (clausing) are first entered on the mate's receipt; these reservations are carried over to the B/L. The Cargo Manifest is the list of all the cargo (by B/L) with port, consignee, quantity and description, and it is the basis of the customs declaration.
Manifestteki hata veya eksiklik, gümrükt: An error or omission in the manifest can lead to a customs fine, the cargo not being released and delay to the ship. The Master confirms that the manifest matches the B/Ls and the actual cargo.
IMDG yük için Dangerous Goods Declaratio: For IMDG cargo, the Dangerous Goods Declaration (DGD), the Container/Vehicle Packing Certificate and correct stowage and segregation documents are mandatory. For bulk cargo, the cargo declaration from the shipper under the IMSBC Code (including the TML/MC information) and, where necessary, a Trimming Certificate are required. Missing documents are a reason for refusing to load.
ORB Part I (machinery space operations): ORB Part I (machinery space operations) and Part II (cargo/ballast — on tankers) are filled in under MARPOL Annex I immediately after each operation, with the relevant coded item (codes A to I in Part I). Discharges of slops, bilge water, sludge and through the oily water separator (15 ppm), internal transfers and deliveries of waste are recorded. Every page is signed by the Master.
ORB tutarsızlığı (örn. sludge üretimi il: An inconsistency in the ORB (e.g. an imbalance between sludge production and delivery or incineration) immediately raises suspicion at PSC and US Coast Guard inspections. Most "magic pipe" (illegal bypass) cases came to light through a contradiction between the ORB and the actual situation.
Garbage Record Book, MARPOL Annex V kaps: The Garbage Record Book keeps records of discharges, incineration and delivery to port reception facilities by garbage category (A–K) under MARPOL Annex V. The Ballast Water Record Book records ballast uptake and discharge, treatment and exchange operations under the BWM Convention. Both books are open to inspection, and gaps in them are a reason for a deficiency.
Crew List, gemideki tüm mürettebatın kim: The Crew List is the official document containing the identity, rank, nationality and certificate details of all the crew on board; immigration and the port authority ask for it on entering port. Under MLC 2006 Standard A2.1, every seafarer's signed SEA must be on board; the Master checks that the SEAs are complete and up to date.
Wages account, allotment kayıtları ve re: Wage records, allotment records and rest hour records are also kept under the MLC. The most frequent MLC findings at PSC are missing SEAs, inconsistencies in wage records and breaches of rest hours.
Mürettebat sertifikaları (CoC, GMDSS, me: The Master keeps a tracking matrix for crew certificates (CoC, GMDSS, medical, STCW courses) and ship certificates (SMC, ISSC, class, statutory). Documents about to expire are included in port and class planning. Sailing with an invalid certificate carries the risk both of PSC detention and of insurance cover being prejudiced (P&I cover prejudice).
Letter of Protest, kaptanın karşı tarafa: A Letter of Protest is the document by which the Master notifies the other party (terminal, charterer, shipper, surveyor) that he or she formally objects to a situation and reserves rights. Typical subjects: cargo damage, a draft survey discrepancy, slow loading or discharging rates, delay due to bad weather, terminal equipment failure, contaminated fuel (bunker dispute). The LOP is given in writing and, if possible, signed by the other party; even if it is refused, the note "presented and refused" is added.
LOP, sea protest'ten farklıdır: sea prot: An LOP is different from a sea protest: a sea protest is a formal declaration made before a notary; an LOP is a commercial means of objection between the parties. The two complement each other.
Kaçak yolcu tespitinde FAL Konvansiyonu: When a stowaway is found, the guidance procedures of the FAL Convention and IMO Res. FAL.13(42) are applied. The Master ensures the person's safety, enters the identity details and the circumstances of discovery on the standard stowaway report form, and notifies the flag state, the next port state, the company and the P&I Club. A stowaway is not made part of the crew; but humane treatment and safety are provided.
Stowaway maliyeti (repatriasyon, fines,: Stowaway costs (repatriation, fines, detention) are generally covered by P&I; early and complete notification is therefore essential for the insurance to respond. Incomplete documentation puts the cover at risk.
ISM Code madde 11, SMS kapsamındaki tüm: ISM Code section 11 requires all documents within the SMS to be current, valid and checked by authorised persons. The removal of invalid or superseded documents, the controlled document list and the tracking of revisions are run under the Master's supervision. Document control discipline is a main focus area in internal and external ISM audits.
Her belge türünün yasal saklama süresi v: Each type of document has a statutory retention period: the ORB 3 years, the garbage record book 2 years, the deck and official log books, depending on the flag state, generally a long time after the event. Completed books are handed over to the company and archived. At a change of Master (handover), all active and completed books, certificates and files of ongoing disputes are handed over to the new Master with a signed record.
Aşağıdaki liste, kaptanın günlük ve lima: The list below summarises the Master's daily and port-by-port document discipline. The list should be adapted to the ship type, the nature of the voyage and the requirements of the flag state.
Belge yönetimi, denizciliğin görünmeyen: Document management is one of the invisible but most decisive disciplines at sea. A well-kept log book is the strongest shield protecting the Master and the company in court; a careless or falsified entry destroys even the best defence. The Master's goal is to turn the principle "every document at the time it happens, as it happens and legibly" into a lasting culture on board.
Pilotun gemiye çıkması, kaptanın sorumlu: The pilot coming on board does not remove the Master's responsibility. The pilot provides local expertise; but the ship's manoeuvring characteristics, her condition and her ultimate safety lie within the Master's knowledge and authority. If the Master considers that a recommendation of the pilot endangers the ship, he or she intervenes.
Pilot köprüüstüne geldiğinde MPX kartı d: When the pilot arrives on the bridge, the MPX card is completed: the passage plan, the speed profile, the expected manoeuvres, the use of tugs, berth or anchorage information, the UKC, weather and current, and the emergency/abort plan are shared. The Master gives the pilot the ship's manoeuvring data (turning circle, stopping distance, draught, propeller and rudder characteristics).
Pilotun planı ile geminin passage plan'ı: If there is a significant difference between the pilot's plan and the ship's passage plan, it is clarified before the manoeuvre begins. "Starting without talking" is a recurring error pattern in investigations of bridge accidents.
Vardiya zabiti, pilotaj boyunca geminin: During pilotage the officer of the watch independently monitors the ship's position (position, speed, rate of turn, UKC) and reports any deviation from the plan to the Master. Helm and engine orders given by the pilot are repeated back (closed loop) and their execution is confirmed. The team supports the pilot not with "blind trust" but with active monitoring.
Pilot biniş/inişi, SOLAS V/23 ve ilgili: The pilot embarks and disembarks by a pilot ladder or combination ladder complying with SOLAS V/23 and the related regulations. The Master verifies that the equipment is rigged correctly and that lighting, a lifebuoy, a heaving line and an attending crew member are ready. Incorrectly rigged pilot ladders are a real and persistent cause of pilot deaths.
Pilotaj/manevra öncesi steering gear tes: Before pilotage or manoeuvring, the steering gear test, the engine being ready for manoeuvring, the anchor stations being ready, the tug-making-fast team and communications are verified. The Master confirms that the bridge team and the forward and aft stations know their duties and are rested.
Kaptan, pilotun bir hareketinin gemiyi t: If the Master becomes convinced that an action of the pilot endangers the ship, he or she intervenes at once and, if necessary, takes the con directly. This is not disrespect towards the pilot but the Master's legal duty. The event is recorded.
Pilotaj, uzmanlık ile nihai sorumluluğun: Pilotage is a delicate process in which expertise and ultimate responsibility work hand in hand. The Master's MPX discipline, active monitoring on the bridge and decisive intervention when needed turn the pilot's local knowledge into a safe passage.
ISM Code madde 4, her şirketin bir veya: ISM Code section 4 requires every company to designate one or more Designated Persons Ashore (DPA). The DPA has two critical features: direct access to the highest level of management, and the task of monitoring the safety and pollution prevention aspects of the ship's operation. The DPA builds a bridge between the Master and the highest level of the company's management; it is a safety line independent of the commercial line (operations, chartering). This independence is designed to stop commercial pressure from overriding safety decisions.
Kaptan, DPA'ya ulaşmak için hiçbir izne: The Master needs no permission to reach the DPA and can do so 24/7, day and night. The DPA's contact details (telephone, e-mail, satellite line) must be posted visibly on the bridge and in the SMS documentation. PSC inspectors often ask "who is the DPA and where is the number?"; crew not knowing this can be raised as an ISM non-conformity.
Overriding authority, kaptanın emniyet,: Overriding authority is the Master's authority to take any decision he or she considers necessary for safety, security and the protection of the marine environment, regardless of the instructions of the company or the charterer. ISM Code 5.2 requires the company to confirm this authority in writing in its SMS. This makes the Master not "the company's order-taker" but the ultimate decision-maker on safety.
Bu yetki soyut bir hak değil, iletişim d: This authority is not an abstract right but a tool tied to communication discipline. When the Master uses the overriding authority, he or she does not simply say "I am not doing it" but notifies the DPA in writing of the reasons, the alternative plan and the risk. Companies examine the records of the use of this authority in ISM internal audits; it never having been used is sometimes regarded as a sign of a "culture of fear".
Emniyet/kirlilik/security olayları emniy: Safety, pollution and security events go through the safety line (DPA); commercial matters (laytime, bunkers, ETA, speed) go through the operations/chartering line. The Master's most frequent mistake is to put a safety event into the commercial line, or a commercial matter into the safety line. This confusion causes both delays in response and a broken chain of legal evidence.
Resmi yazışmalar (port authority, flag s: Official correspondence (port authority, flag state, class, customs) usually goes through the agent or directly over the Master's signature. Every statement made to third parties (terminal, the charterer's surveyor, an inspector) must be measured and documented, because it can bind the company legally.
Denizcilikte sözlü iletişim kanıt değild: At sea, oral communication is not evidence. The Master's basic principle: "if you said it, write it down; if you did not write it, it counts as not said." Every critical communication is recorded by e-mail, in the log book, in the SOF (Statement of Facts), in a Letter of Protest or by telex. Telephone conversations are confirmed at once by e-mail as a summary ("as per our telcon at 0930 LT...").
Belge zinciri ileride doğacak demurrage,: The chain of documents is the strongest defence protecting the Master and the company in later demurrage, off-hire, cargo damage or accident disputes. Time stamps (UTC and LT together), position, weather and the counterpart must always be stated. Back-dating documents, on the other hand, is a serious disciplinary and legal offence; when courts detect it, the credibility of all the records collapses.
Time charter'da (örn. NYPE, SHELLTIME) c: Under a time charter (e.g. NYPE, SHELLTIME) the charterer hires the ship for a certain period and directs her commercial use (employment). Under clause 8 of the NYPE, the Master must follow the charterer's orders "as regards employment, agency or other arrangements"; but this obligation does NOT extend to the safe navigation of the ship, navigation as such, or the Master's overriding authority. The charterer decides the route, port and speed commercially; the Master remains responsible for navigational safety.
Time charter'da \"off-hire\" (kira durma: The concept of "off-hire" is critical under a time charter: if the ship cannot perform her service because of a breakdown, a shortage of crew or the Master's fault, the charterer may stop paying hire. This is why the Master's accurate and timely reporting of delays, engine failures, deviations and similar situations directly affects the company's income. The "safe port / safe berth" warranty also lies with the charterer; the Master objects to an order to an unsafe port and issues a Letter of Protest.
Voyage charter'da (örn. GENCON) armatör: Under a voyage charter (e.g. GENCON) the shipowner charters the ship to carry a certain cargo from A to B; the commercial management remains largely with the shipowner. Here the Master's main contact with the charterer revolves around the NOR (Notice of Readiness), laytime and demurrage. A validly tendered NOR (the ship ready "in all respects") starts the laytime clock; an early or invalid NOR is a main subject of demurrage claims.
Kaptan, voyage charter'da SOF'u (Stateme: Under a voyage charter the Master keeps the SOF (Statement of Facts) meticulously: NOR tendered/accepted times, pilot on/off, all fast, hose connected, commenced/completed loading, weather stoppages, equipment breakdowns. The demurrage/despatch calculation is made entirely from these records. Every "remark" in the SOF signed with the charterer's surveyor can make a difference of thousands of dollars later.
Charterer'in voyage instructions'ı (rota: The charterer's voyage instructions (route, speed, ECO speed, weather routing service, bunker port) are commercially binding; but no instruction that endangers safety is binding. When the Master faces an unsafe instruction, he or she asks for the instruction in writing, gives a reasoned refusal in writing, proposes an alternative and informs the DPA. Saying "no" protects the Master when it is done professionally and with documents; done argumentatively and orally, it leaves the Master on his or her own.
Pratikte en sık çatışma \"unsafe port /: In practice the most frequent clashes arise over "unsafe port / unsafe berth", "keeping the ETA with excessive speed" and "continuing the voyage with deficient equipment". In these situations the Master puts safety first; the commercial consequence (off-hire, demurrage) is settled between the company's lawyers and the charterer, but the loss of life or of the ship cannot be undone.
Liman acentesi, gemiyi limanda temsil ed: The port agent is the party who represents the ship in port, arranges the pilot and tugs, handles customs and immigration formalities, and coordinates supplies (provisions, bunkers, fresh water), waste collection, crew changes and the flow of documents. The agent is sometimes appointed by the shipowner (owner's agent) and sometimes by the charterer (charterer's agent); this distinction matters where interests clash. Since the charterer's agent is commercially tied to the charterer, the Master must not relax record discipline in protecting the interests of the ship and the shipowner.
Kaptan, acenteye pre-arrival mesajı ile: Through a pre-arrival message the Master informs the agent of the ETA, draught, gross and net tonnage, the last 10 ports, the crew list, waste quantities, supply requirements and special requests (MEDEVAC, repatriation, spare parts). He or she asks for all the agent's expenses to be documented transparently with the PDA/FDA (Proforma / Final Disbursement Account) and questions suspicious items.
IMO FAL Convention (Convention on Facili: The IMO FAL Convention (Convention on Facilitation of International Maritime Traffic) defines the standard documents: the General Declaration, Cargo Declaration, Ship's Stores Declaration, Crew's Effects Declaration, Crew List, Passenger List, Dangerous Goods and the Maritime Declaration of Health. The Master is responsible for the accuracy of these documents; a missing or false declaration leads to customs fines and delays. Since 2024 many ports require electronic declarations through a Maritime Single Window.
Kaptan, acente aracılığıyla yürütülse de: Although the FAL documents are handled through the agent, the Master must check their content because he or she signs them personally. In particular, undeclared tobacco, alcohol or cash in the Ship's Stores and Crew's Effects declarations leads to heavy fines ("manifest violation") in the USA and many other countries. Passport and seaman's book details in the Crew List are critical for immigration.
PSC denetimleri (Paris MoU, Tokyo MoU, U: During PSC inspections (Paris MoU, Tokyo MoU, USCG, etc.) the Master is the inspector's only official counterpart. Open, honest and documented communication is essential; hiding documents or misleading the inspector makes a detention worse. Every deficiency on Form A/B issued at the end of the inspection is recorded with a code; code "30 — detainable" means the ship is detained. The Master reports the findings at once to the DPA and the technical department and coordinates the corrective action plan with the company.
Kaptan, haksız gördüğü bir detention'a k: The Master can use the right of appeal against a detention he or she considers unjust through the flag state and the company; but moving the ship without the inspector's permission during this process is a serious violation. The appeal, too, proceeds with documents and reasons.
Bayrak devleti idaresi (Flag State) ve k: Communication with the flag state administration (Flag State) and the class society (ABS, DNV, LR, BV, ClassNK, etc.) concerns the validity of certificates, survey planning, condition reports, casualty reports and deficiencies. In a serious accident the Master makes the mandatory casualty report to the flag state under SOLAS I/21 and MARPOL. This report later forms the basis of the MAIB/IMO casualty investigation.
Kaptan, sertifikaların (Safety Construct: The Master tracks the validity dates and survey windows of the certificates (Safety Construction, Safety Equipment, Safety Radio, IOPP, ISM/SMC, ISSC, MLC/DMLC); an expired or conditional certificate is a reason for PSC detention. "Condition of class" (CoC) items identified in communication with the class surveyor are closed in time.
Communication with the terminal is safety-critical. On tankers, under ISGOTT the Ship-Shore Safety Checklist is completed after berthing and confirmed every watch; at the pre-transfer conference the loading rate, the maximum pressure, the ESD (Emergency Shut Down) signal, the communication failure procedure and the authority to stop are agreed. The Master says "no" with overriding authority to an unsafe request from the terminal representative (e.g. starting transfer before the checklist is completed).
Bulk ve genel kargoda BLU Code (Code of: For bulk and general cargo, agreement is reached with the terminal on the loading plan, sequence and rate within the framework of the BLU Code (Code of Practice for the Safe Loading and Unloading of Bulk Carriers). An excessive loading rate or a wrong sequence by the terminal carries a risk of exceeding strength limits; the Master and the Chief Officer agree the authority to stop with the terminal from the outset.
Petrol/kimyasal tankerlerde OCIMF SIRE 2: For oil and chemical tankers the OCIMF SIRE 2.0 inspection, and for dry cargo the RightShip inspection, are decisive for the ship's commercial survival. The Master communicates with the vetting inspector professionally and well prepared; he or she meets observations not with defence but with explanation and corrective action. Negative observations in the vetting report can lead to the charterer rejecting the ship (vetting rejection); this directly affects the company's income.
Cargo surveyor, draft surveyor, bunker s: Every joint measurement or signature with the cargo surveyor, draft surveyor, bunker surveyor and P&I surveyor can bind the company. On a measurement or statement he or she does not agree with, the Master adds the remark "for receipt only" / "under protest" and issues a Letter of Protest. Oral admissions made to a surveyor can later become evidence against the ship.
Ciddi kazada (çatışma, oturma, yangın, k: In a serious accident (collision, grounding, fire, pollution, loss of life, piracy), the order of communication must have been memorised in advance: first the safety of life and the MRCC/MAYDAY, then the DPA, then the flag state and P&I, then the charterer and the agent. The company's Emergency Response Plan (ERP) typically defines an Emergency Response Team (ERT) and a 24/7 hotline. The Master's task is to pass on the reality on site quickly, accurately and without exaggeration, and not to speculate.
Kirlilik olayında SOPEP/SMPEP devreye gi: In a pollution incident the SOPEP/SMPEP comes into effect; the coastal state, the port authority and P&I are informed at once. In US waters, under OPA 90, notifying the QI (Qualified Individual) and the OSRO is time-critical; delay multiplies the penalty. In the first report the Master uses the framework "estimated quantity, source, measures taken, assistance needed".
Kaza sonrası kaptan ve mürettebat, medya: After an accident the Master and the crew make NO statements to the media, to shore surveyors, to the other party's lawyers or on social media. All external communication goes through the spokesperson appointed by the company and through P&I and the lawyers. An early and thoughtless sentence ("I think the speed was too high") becomes evidence against the ship in criminal and compensation cases. This discipline is explained to the crew beforehand in a briefing.
Kaptan, resmi soruşturma (flag, coastal,: The Master is honest in statements to official investigations (flag, coastal state, MAIB) but knows the right to avoid, without legal advice, statements amounting to an admission of guilt. In many countries the criminalisation of the Master after an accident (criminalization of seafarers) is a real risk; the P&I "loss prevention" department provides legal support on this.
ISPS Code çerçevesinde gemide Ship Secur: Under the ISPS Code there is a Ship Security Officer (SSO) on board and a Company Security Officer (CSO) ashore. The Master coordinates with the SSO and CSO on security matters; but the ISPS Code (and SOLAS XI-2/8) makes clear that no one may constrain the decisions the Master considers necessary for the safety and security of the ship. The Security Level (1/2/3) is set by the flag or coastal state; a change of level is passed to the ship at once and the appropriate measures (access control, patrols, restricted areas) are stepped up.
Ship Security Alert System (SSAS) tetikl: When the Ship Security Alert System (SSAS) is activated, the signal goes silently to the CSO and the flag state; no alarm sounds on the bridge (so that pirates do not notice). The Master knows the SSAS test and activation procedure, the conditions for issuing a declaration of security (DoS) and the reporting for high risk area (HRA) transits (UKMTO, MSCHOA).
Yüksek riskli bölgelerde (Aden Körfezi,: In high-risk areas (the Gulf of Aden, the Gulf of Guinea, the approaches to the Singapore Strait), the Master carries out, within the BMP (Best Management Practices) framework, reporting to UKMTO, hardening measures (razor wire, citadel, water hoses), group transits/convoys and, if necessary, coordination of an armed security team (PCASP). All this coordination is planned in advance with the CSO and the company.
Korsan saldırısı anında iletişim sırası:: Order of communication during a pirate attack: UKMTO/MSCHOA, the navy, the CSO/DPA, the flag state. The Master's decision to withdraw to the citadel is the most effective way of protecting the crew's lives; but the citadel's communication and endurance criteria must be tested in advance.
Kaptanın iletişim altyapısı GMDSS (DSC,: The Master's communication infrastructure covers GMDSS (DSC, Inmarsat-C, MF/HF/VHF, EPIRB, SART) and commercial satellite systems (FleetBroadband, VSAT, Starlink and similar). In distress, urgency and safety traffic the correct channel and procedure are vital: MAYDAY (distress), PAN-PAN (urgency), SECURITE (safety). The listening watch on VHF Ch 16 and the discipline of Ch 13 (bridge-to-bridge manoeuvring) are a daily routine at sea.
Ticari e-posta ve uydu hattının ucuzlama: Cheaper commercial e-mail and satellite lines have made communication easier but have also created pressure to "ask about everything instantly". The Master handles routine commercial traffic with economy/store-and-forward systems and urgent safety traffic over a real-time channel; he or she does not mix the two. In terms of cyber security, he or she verifies messages against the risk of e-mail phishing and fake instructions (especially bunker and payment fraud).
Resmi yevmiye (Official Log Book), deck: The Official Log Book, deck log, bell book, GMDSS log, oil record book, garbage record book and rest hour records are the written backbone of the Master's communication discipline. These records are the "single source of truth" between the ship and the outside world and can be asked for at any time by PSC, vetting or insurers. The VDR (Voyage Data Recorder), for its part, is the most reliable evidence after an accident; in an accident, preserving the VDR data (save/preserve) is among the Master's first tasks.
Kayıtların tutarlılığı kritiktir: deck l: Consistency of records is critical: the position in the deck log, the ECDIS, the GPS and the SOF must not contradict each other. A contradiction leads an investigation to conclude that "the records are unreliable" and destroys the insurance defence. The Master periodically cross-checks the consistency of the records.
Kaptanın iletişim becerisi, \"kibar yazı: The Master's communication skill is not "polite correspondence" but the discipline of passing the right message to the right party at the right time, with documents. Keeping the DPA line alive, managing charterer pressure professionally and maintaining the discipline of signatures and statements towards third parties protect the Master both legally and in terms of safety. The principle not to be forgotten is this: commercial pressure is temporary, but the accident and legal consequences of badly managed communication are permanent. A seasoned Master is the one who, even at moments when saying "yes" is easy, can say the "no" that safety requires, with reasons and with documents.
